- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

1	# Developer Walk-Me Guide
2	### How to run, test, and change autom9
3	
4	This guide assumes you have Docker, Node.js, and `uv` installed but limited familiarity with the codebase. It covers everything from first boot to making and verifying a code change.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. What the project is
9	
10	autom9 is two things that work together:
11	
12	| Part | What it is | Where it lives |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Backend** | A Python/FastAPI REST API | `autom9-backend/` |
15	| **Extension** | A Tableau extension (Svelte/TypeScript UI) | `autom9-extension/` |
16	
17	The backend is what you'll spend most of your time on. It connects to a Postgres database, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools like Smartsheet and Google Calendar.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. First-time setup
22	
23	### 2a. Environment file
24	
25	The backend needs secrets to start. Copy the example and fill in the two required values:
26	
27	```bash
28	cp autom9-backend/.env.example autom9-backend/.env
29	```
30	
31	Edit `autom9-backend/.env` — the only two lines that need real values for local dev:
32	
33	```
34	ENCRYPTION_KEY=<any 32-byte base64 string>
35	BACKEND_SECRET=<any string you choose, e.g. "localdev">
36	```
37	
38	To generate a valid `ENCRYPTION_KEY`:
39	```bash
40	uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
41	```
42	Run that from `autom9-backend/`. Paste the output into `.env`.
43	
44	### 2b. Start the database
45	
46	```bash
47	docker-compose up db
48	```
49	
50	This starts a Postgres 16 container on port 5432. Leave it running in a terminal.
51	
52	### 2c. Run database migrations
53	
54	```bash
55	cd autom9-backend
56	uv run alembic upgrade head
57	```
58	
59	This creates all the tables. You only need to do this once (and again after any migration files are added).
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 3. Running the backend
64	
65	```bash
66	cd autom9-backend
67	uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
68	```
69	
70	`--reload` means the server restarts automatically when you save a Python file — you don't need to restart it manually after changes.
71	
72	The API is now at `http://localhost:8000`. Check it's working:
73	
74	```bash
75	curl http://localhost:8000/health
76	# → {"status":"ok"}
77	```
78	
79	Interactive API docs (great for exploring endpoints):
80	```
81	http://localhost:8000/docs
82	```
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 4. Running the tests
87	
88	All backend tests live in `autom9-backend/tests/`. **Tests do not need the backend server running** — they spin up their own in-memory app. They do need Postgres running (`docker-compose up db`).
89	
90	### Run everything:
91	```bash
92	cd autom9-backend
93	uv run pytest -v
94	```
95	
96	### Run a single test file:
97	```bash
98	uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
99	```
100	
101	### Run a single test by name:
102	```bash
103	uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py::test_health_check_ok -v
104	```
105	
106	### Run with coverage (see which lines are untested):
107	```bash
108	uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing
109	```
110	
111	**Always use `uv run` prefix** — do not use `python`, `python3`, or bare `pytest`.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. How the tests work
116	
117	You don't need a real LLM key or real Google Calendar credentials to run tests. The tests use **mocks** — fake stand-ins that simulate the external services.
118	
119	The test setup (`tests/conftest.py`) automatically:
120	- Generates a throwaway encryption key
121	- Points to a local test database (`autom9_test`)
122	- Creates all tables before tests and drops them after
123	- Wraps each test in a transaction that rolls back — so tests never leave dirty data
124	
125	If a test uses the HTTP client, it goes through the real FastAPI app but with a fake database session injected. No real HTTP calls are made to Google, Smartsheet, etc. unless you explicitly write a test that does so.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 6. Project layout (the parts you'll touch)
130	
131	```
132	autom9-backend/
133	├── app/
134	│   ├── api/                  ← HTTP endpoints (routes, request handling)
135	│   │   ├── chat.py           ← The main chat + tool-confirmation flow
136	│   │   ├── integrations.py   ← Health check endpoints
137	│   │   └── admin/            ← Admin routes (credentials, config, logs)
138	│   ├── integrations/         ← External service clients
139	│   │   ├── base.py           ← Interface every integration must implement
140	│   │   ├── google_calendar.py← Google Calendar (story 3.6)
141	│   │   ├── smartsheet.py     ← Smartsheet (story 3.5)
142	│   │   └── __init__.py       ← Registry of all integrations
143	│   ├── agent/
144	│   │   ├── masking.py        ← PII token masking / rehydration
145	│   │   └── provider_factory.py← LLM provider loader
146	│   ├── core/
147	│   │   ├── config.py         ← All env vars live here (Settings class)
148	│   │   └── exceptions.py     ← Custom exceptions (IntegrationError, etc.)
149	│   ├── models/               ← Database table definitions (SQLAlchemy)
150	│   └── schemas/              ← Request/response shapes (Pydantic)
151	└── tests/                    ← Mirror of app/ — one test file per module
152	```
153	
154	**Rule of thumb:** when you change a file in `app/integrations/`, the corresponding test is in `tests/integrations/`. Same pattern everywhere.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 7. Making a code change — end to end
159	
160	Here's the full loop for a typical change.
161	
162	### Step 1 — Find the file
163	
164	If you're changing how Google Calendar works: `app/integrations/google_calendar.py`.  
165	If you're adding an env var: `app/core/config.py` (add it to the `Settings` class).  
166	If you're changing an API endpoint: `app/api/<relevant_file>.py`.
167	
168	### Step 2 — Make the change
169	
170	Edit the file. The server reloads automatically (if it's running with `--reload`).
171	
172	### Step 3 — Run the relevant tests
173	
174	```bash
175	cd autom9-backend
176	uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
177	```
178	
179	If tests fail, the output will show you exactly which assertion failed and on which line.
180	
181	### Step 4 — Run the full suite
182	
183	```bash
184	uv run pytest -v
185	```
186	
187	207 tests should pass. If something outside your file broke, you'll see it here.
188	
189	### Step 5 — Manual smoke test (optional)
190	
191	With the server running (`uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload`), you can hit the API directly:
192	
193	```bash
194	# Check all integration health statuses
195	curl http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/status
196	
197	# Check a specific integration (requires admin header)
198	curl -H "X-Autom9-Admin: <your BACKEND_SECRET>" \
199	     http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/test/google_calendar
200	```
201	
202	---
203	
204	## 8. Adding a new env var
205	
206	1. Open `app/core/config.py`
207	2. Add a field to the `Settings` class:
208	   ```python
209	   MY_NEW_VAR: str | None = None      # optional
210	   MY_REQUIRED_VAR: str = "default"   # with default
211	   ```
212	3. Add it to `autom9-backend/.env` (and `.env.example`)
213	4. Access it anywhere in the app: `from app.core.config import settings` then `settings.MY_NEW_VAR`
214	
215	---
216	
217	## 9. Adding a new integration
218	
219	All integrations follow the same pattern as `google_calendar.py`:
220	
221	1. Create `app/integrations/my_service.py`
222	2. Inherit from `IntegrationBase` (defined in `app/integrations/base.py`)
223	3. Implement `name`, `health_check()`, and `execute(action, params)`
224	4. Register it in `app/integrations/__init__.py` by adding it to `ALL_INTEGRATIONS`
225	5. Create `tests/integrations/test_my_service.py` — mock `httpx.AsyncClient` to avoid real HTTP calls
226	
227	The `health_check()` method **must never raise** — always return an `IntegrationStatus`. The `execute()` method raises `IntegrationError` on failure.
228	
229	---
230	
231	## 10. Common commands cheat sheet
232	
233	```bash
234	# Start the database
235	docker-compose up db
236	
237	# Start the backend server (auto-reloads on change)
238	cd autom9-backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
239	
240	# Run all tests
241	cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest -v
242	
243	# Run one test file
244	cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
245	
246	# Run migrations after pulling new changes
247	cd autom9-backend && uv run alembic upgrade head
248	
249	# Generate a new encryption key
250	cd autom9-backend && uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
251	
252	# Check test coverage for a module
253	cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest --cov=app/integrations --cov-report=term-missing
254	```
255	
256	---
257	
258	## 11. When something goes wrong
259	
260	| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
261	|---|---|---|
262	| `connection refused` on port 5432 | Postgres not running | `docker-compose up db` |
263	| `ENCRYPTION_KEY not set` on startup | Missing `.env` | Copy `.env.example`, generate key |
264	| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Dependencies not installed | `uv sync` from `autom9-backend/` |
265	| Test fails with `IntegrationError` unexpectedly | Monkeypatch not setting all credentials | Check `_configured()` helper in the test |
266	| Alembic complains about head | New migration added by someone else | `uv run alembic upgrade head` |

# Developer Walk-Me Guide
### How to run, test, and change autom9

This guide assumes you have Docker, Node.js, and `uv` installed but limited familiarity with the codebase. It covers everything from first boot to making and verifying a code change.

---

## 1. What the project is

autom9 is two things that work together:

| Part | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Backend** | A Python/FastAPI REST API | `autom9-backend/` |
| **Extension** | A Tableau extension (Svelte/TypeScript UI) | `autom9-extension/` |

The backend is what you'll spend most of your time on. It connects to a Postgres database, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools like Smartsheet and Google Calendar.

---

## 2. First-time setup

### 2a. Environment file

The backend needs secrets to start. Copy the example and fill in the two required values:

```bash
cp autom9-backend/.env.example autom9-backend/.env
```

Edit `autom9-backend/.env` — the only two lines that need real values for local dev:

```
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<any 32-byte base64 string>
BACKEND_SECRET=<any string you choose, e.g. "localdev">
```

To generate a valid `ENCRYPTION_KEY`:
```bash
uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```
Run that from `autom9-backend/`. Paste the output into `.env`.

### 2b. Start the database

```bash
docker-compose up db
```

This starts a Postgres 16 container on port 5432. Leave it running in a terminal.

### 2c. Run database migrations

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

This creates all the tables. You only need to do this once (and again after any migration files are added).

---

## 3. Running the backend

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

`--reload` means the server restarts automatically when you save a Python file — you don't need to restart it manually after changes.

The API is now at `http://localhost:8000`. Check it's working:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

Interactive API docs (great for exploring endpoints):
```
http://localhost:8000/docs
```

---

## 4. Running the tests

All backend tests live in `autom9-backend/tests/`. **Tests do not need the backend server running** — they spin up their own in-memory app. They do need Postgres running (`docker-compose up db`).

### Run everything:
```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest -v
```

### Run a single test file:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
```

### Run a single test by name:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py::test_health_check_ok -v
```

### Run with coverage (see which lines are untested):
```bash
uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing
```

**Always use `uv run` prefix** — do not use `python`, `python3`, or bare `pytest`.

---

## 5. How the tests work

You don't need a real LLM key or real Google Calendar credentials to run tests. The tests use **mocks** — fake stand-ins that simulate the external services.

The test setup (`tests/conftest.py`) automatically:
- Generates a throwaway encryption key
- Points to a local test database (`autom9_test`)
- Creates all tables before tests and drops them after
- Wraps each test in a transaction that rolls back — so tests never leave dirty data

If a test uses the HTTP client, it goes through the real FastAPI app but with a fake database session injected. No real HTTP calls are made to Google, Smartsheet, etc. unless you explicitly write a test that does so.

---

## 6. Project layout (the parts you'll touch)

```
autom9-backend/
├── app/
│   ├── api/                  ← HTTP endpoints (routes, request handling)
│   │   ├── chat.py           ← The main chat + tool-confirmation flow
│   │   ├── integrations.py   ← Health check endpoints
│   │   └── admin/            ← Admin routes (credentials, config, logs)
│   ├── integrations/         ← External service clients
│   │   ├── base.py           ← Interface every integration must implement
│   │   ├── google_calendar.py← Google Calendar (story 3.6)
│   │   ├── smartsheet.py     ← Smartsheet (story 3.5)
│   │   └── __init__.py       ← Registry of all integrations
│   ├── agent/
│   │   ├── masking.py        ← PII token masking / rehydration
│   │   └── provider_factory.py← LLM provider loader
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── config.py         ← All env vars live here (Settings class)
│   │   └── exceptions.py     ← Custom exceptions (IntegrationError, etc.)
│   ├── models/               ← Database table definitions (SQLAlchemy)
│   └── schemas/              ← Request/response shapes (Pydantic)
└── tests/                    ← Mirror of app/ — one test file per module
```

**Rule of thumb:** when you change a file in `app/integrations/`, the corresponding test is in `tests/integrations/`. Same pattern everywhere.

---

## 7. Making a code change — end to end

Here's the full loop for a typical change.

### Step 1 — Find the file

If you're changing how Google Calendar works: `app/integrations/google_calendar.py`.  
If you're adding an env var: `app/core/config.py` (add it to the `Settings` class).  
If you're changing an API endpoint: `app/api/<relevant_file>.py`.

### Step 2 — Make the change

Edit the file. The server reloads automatically (if it's running with `--reload`).

### Step 3 — Run the relevant tests

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
```

If tests fail, the output will show you exactly which assertion failed and on which line.

### Step 4 — Run the full suite

```bash
uv run pytest -v
```

207 tests should pass. If something outside your file broke, you'll see it here.

### Step 5 — Manual smoke test (optional)

With the server running (`uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload`), you can hit the API directly:

```bash
# Check all integration health statuses
curl http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/status

# Check a specific integration (requires admin header)
curl -H "X-Autom9-Admin: <your BACKEND_SECRET>" \
     http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/test/google_calendar
```

---

## 8. Adding a new env var

1. Open `app/core/config.py`
2. Add a field to the `Settings` class:
   ```python
   MY_NEW_VAR: str | None = None      # optional
   MY_REQUIRED_VAR: str = "default"   # with default
   ```
3. Add it to `autom9-backend/.env` (and `.env.example`)
4. Access it anywhere in the app: `from app.core.config import settings` then `settings.MY_NEW_VAR`

---

## 9. Adding a new integration

All integrations follow the same pattern as `google_calendar.py`:

1. Create `app/integrations/my_service.py`
2. Inherit from `IntegrationBase` (defined in `app/integrations/base.py`)
3. Implement `name`, `health_check()`, and `execute(action, params)`
4. Register it in `app/integrations/__init__.py` by adding it to `ALL_INTEGRATIONS`
5. Create `tests/integrations/test_my_service.py` — mock `httpx.AsyncClient` to avoid real HTTP calls

The `health_check()` method **must never raise** — always return an `IntegrationStatus`. The `execute()` method raises `IntegrationError` on failure.

---

## 10. Common commands cheat sheet

```bash
# Start the database
docker-compose up db

# Start the backend server (auto-reloads on change)
cd autom9-backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Run all tests
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest -v

# Run one test file

# Developer Walk-Me Guide
### How to navigate, test, and extend autom9

This guide assumes you have Docker, Node.js, and `uv` installed but limited familiarity with the codebase. It covers first boot, making and verifying a code change, and how all the pieces connect.

---

## 1. What the project is

autom9 is two things:

| Part | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Backend** | Python/FastAPI REST API | `autom9-backend/` |
| **Extension** | Tableau extension (Svelte/TypeScript UI) | `autom9-extension/` |

The backend connects to Postgres, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools (Google Calendar, Google Docs, Smartsheet). The extension is embedded inside Tableau and calls the backend API.

---

## 2. First-time setup

### 2a. Environment file

```bash
cp autom9-backend/.env.example autom9-backend/.env
```

The only two values you need to fill in for local dev:

```
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<any 32-byte base64 string>
BACKEND_SECRET=<any string, e.g. "localdev">
```

Generate a valid encryption key:
```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```

### 2b. Start the database

```bash
docker-compose up db
```

Starts Postgres 16 on port 5432. Leave it running.

### 2c. Run migrations

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

Only needed once, then again after anyone adds migration files.

---

## 3. Running the backend

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

`--reload` restarts automatically on every Python file save.

Health check:
```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

Interactive API explorer (browse and call all endpoints):
```
http://localhost:8000/docs
```

---

## 4. Running the frontend (extension)

```bash
cp autom9-extension/.env.example autom9-extension/.env
# VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000 (already correct for local dev)

cd autom9-extension
npm install
npm run dev
```

Dev server starts at `http://localhost:5173`. This runs outside Tableau — some Tableau-specific features will be stubbed, but the panels and API calls work.

---

## 5. Running the tests

Tests live in `autom9-backend/tests/`. They **do not need the server running** — they spin up their own in-memory app. They **do need Postgres running** (`docker-compose up db`).

```bash
# Run everything
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest -v

# Run one file
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v

# Run one test by name
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py::test_health_check_ok -v

# Coverage — see which lines are untested
uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing
```

**Always use `uv run`** — never bare `python`, `python3`, or `pytest`.

---

## 6. How the tests work

No real LLM keys or Google credentials are needed. Every external call is **mocked** — the tests use fake stand-ins that simulate the real services.

`tests/conftest.py` does this automatically for every test:
- Generates a throwaway `ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- Points to `autom9_test` (a separate local database)
- Creates all tables before the suite starts, drops them after
- Wraps each test in a transaction that **rolls back** — dirty data never persists between tests

When you write a test against the HTTP client, it runs through the real FastAPI app with a fake database session injected. No HTTP calls go to Google, Smartsheet, etc. unless you write one that explicitly does.

---

## 7. Full project layout

```
autom9-backend/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py               ← FastAPI app bootstrap, router registration, CORS
│   ├── api/                  ← HTTP endpoints (routes, request handling)
│   │   ├── chat.py           ← Main chat + tool-confirmation flow
│   │   ├── data.py           ← Public data endpoints: /tasks, /open-work
│   │   ├── integrations.py   ← Integration health-check endpoints
│   │   ├── sessions.py       ← Session creation
│   │   ├── status.py         ← Global status endpoint
│   │   └── admin/            ← Admin routes (credentials, config, logs)
│   ├── agent/                ← LLM abstraction layer
│   │   ├── masking.py        ← PII token masking / rehydration
│   │   └── provider_factory.py ← Loads Anthropic or OpenAI provider
│   ├── config/               ← Workflow configuration system
│   │   └── workflow_schema.py ← Pydantic validation models for workflow JSON
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── config.py         ← All env vars (Settings class, read from .env)
│   │   └── exceptions.py     ← Custom exceptions (IntegrationError, etc.)
│   ├── db/                   ← Database layer
│   │   ├── engine.py         ← Async SQLAlchemy engine setup
│   │   └── dependencies.py   ← FastAPI get_db() dependency
│   ├── integrations/         ← External service clients
│   │   ├── base.py           ← Abstract interface every integration must implement
│   │   ├── google_calendar.py← Google Calendar (create invites)
│   │   ├── google_docs.py    ← Google Docs (fetch tasks, fetch open work)
│   │   ├── smartsheet.py     ← Smartsheet
│   │   └── __init__.py       ← ALL_INTEGRATIONS registry
│   ├── models/               ← SQLAlchemy ORM table definitions
│   ├── schemas/              ← Pydantic request/response shapes
│   │   ├── data.py           ← TaskItem, TasksResponse, OpportunityItem, OpenWorkResponse
│   │   └── status.py         ← Meta, StatusResponse
│   └── services/             ← Business logic helpers
│       └── encryption.py     ← Fernet-based credential encryption
└── tests/                    ← One file per app module
    ├── conftest.py           ← Fixtures: engine, db_session, client
    ├── agent/                ← Tests for provider implementations and masking
    ├── api/                  ← Tests for every API route
    │   ├── test_data.py      ← Tests for /api/data/tasks and /api/data/open-work
    │   └── test_open_work.py ← Additional open-work behaviour tests
    ├── config/               ← Tests for workflow config validation
    └── integrations/         ← Tests for each external service client

autom9-extension/src/
├── App.svelte                ← Root component: init, routing, shell
├── main.ts                   ← Vite entry point
├── app.css                   ← Global styles
├── components/
│   ├── DataPanel.svelte      ← Task list fetched from /api/data/tasks
│   ├── OpenWorkPanel.svelte  ← Opportunities fetched from /api/data/open-work
│   ├── ChatPanel.svelte      ← Chat interface
│   ├── StatusBar.svelte      ← Integration health badges
│   ├── AdminConfig.svelte    ← Admin panel (shown with ?admin query param)
│   ├── WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte ← Edit workflow JSON in-browser
│   ├── ActionConfirm.svelte  ← Tool-use confirmation dialog
│   ├── InputBar.svelte       ← Chat input field
│   └── MessageList.svelte    ← Chat history
├── lib/
│   ├── api.ts                ← Typed API client (all fetch calls go here)
│   └── tableau.ts            ← Tableau extension runtime shim
└── stores/
    ├── session.svelte.ts     ← Session ID, Tableau user ID
    ├── status.svelte.ts      ← Integration statuses
    ├── chat.svelte.ts        ← Chat messages and streaming state
    └── data.svelte.ts        ← Task and opportunity data
```

**Rule of thumb:** when you change `app/integrations/google_docs.py`, the test is `tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py`. Same pattern everywhere.

---

## 8. How a request travels end to end

Take **"load open work opportunities"** as a concrete example:

1. `OpenWorkPanel.svelte` mounts → calls `lib/api.ts` → `GET /api/data/open-work`
2. `app/api/data.py` handles the route:
   - reads `open_work_board.google_docs_url` from the active workflow config
   - calls `GoogleDocsIntegration().execute("fetch_open_work", {"url": ...})`
3. `app/integrations/google_docs.py`:
   - refreshes the OAuth2 access token (cached, thread-safe)
   - fetches the Google Doc via the Docs API
   - parses section headers (`Billable` / `Internal`) into structured items
4. Route handler maps the result to `OpenWorkResponse` (Pydantic schema in `app/schemas/data.py`)
5. JSON response returns → `OpenWorkPanel` renders badge + title for each item

To understand **any** feature, follow this same path: frontend component → `lib/api.ts` → backend route (`app/api/`) → integration or service → schema.

---

## 9. The workflow config system

Each "workflow" is a JSON blob stored in the database that tells the agent:
- What tools it can call (`tools` list)
- What instructions to follow (`agent_instructions`)
- Where to read task data (`data_panel.google_docs_url`)
- Where to read open work (`open_work_board.google_docs_url`)

`app/config/workflow_schema.py` validates this JSON using Pydantic. Key model:

```python
class WorkflowConfigSchema(BaseModel):
    version: str              # semver, e.g. "1.0.0"
    workflow_id: str          # unique identifier
    tools: list[ToolDefinition]
    agent_instructions: str
    data_panel: DataPanelConfig | None
    open_work_board: OpenWorkBoardConfig | None
```

Each `ToolDefinition` maps a tool name → integration name → action string, which is how the chat agent knows to call `GoogleCalendarIntegration.execute("create_invite", ...)` when the LLM invokes the `create_calendar_invite` tool.

You can edit the active workflow config at runtime through the `AdminConfig` panel (visible when the extension URL has `?admin` in it).

---

## 10. The integration system

All integrations implement the same three-method contract (`app/integrations/base.py`):

```python
class IntegrationBase(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str: ...         # e.g. "google_calendar"

    async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus: ...
    # NEVER raises — always returns status="healthy" or status="unavailable"

    async def execute(self, action: str, params: dict) -> dict: ...
    # Raises IntegrationError on failure — caught at the API layer → HTTP 503
```

Registered integrations (from `app/integrations/__init__.py`):

| Integration | `name` | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| `GoogleCalendarIntegration` | `google_calendar` | `create_invite` |
| `GoogleDocsIntegration` | `google_docs` | `fetch_tasks`, `fetch_open_work` |
| `SmartsheetIntegration` | `smartsheet` | (various) |
| `TableauDataIntegration` | `tableau` | (placeholder) |

---

## 11. Making a code change — end to end

### Step 1 — Find the file

| What you're changing | Where to look |
|---|---|
| API endpoint | `app/api/<name>.py` |
| Integration logic | `app/integrations/<name>.py` |
| Request/response shape | `app/schemas/<name>.py` |
| Env var | `app/core/config.py` → `Settings` class |
| Workflow config structure | `app/config/workflow_schema.py` |
| Frontend component | `autom9-extension/src/components/<Name>.svelte` |
| API calls from frontend | `autom9-extension/src/lib/api.ts` |

### Step 2 — Make the change

Edit the file. The server reloads automatically (if running with `--reload`).

### Step 3 — Run the relevant tests

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py -v
```

Test output shows exactly which assertion failed and on which line.

### Step 4 — Run the full suite

```bash
uv run pytest -v
```

If something outside your file breaks, you'll see it here.

### Step 5 — Manual smoke test (optional)

```bash
# Check all integration statuses
curl http://localhost:8000/api/status

# Fetch open-work data (requires active workflow config with open_work_board set)
curl http://localhost:8000/api/data/open-work

# Fetch task list
curl http://localhost:8000/api/data/tasks

# Test a specific integration (requires admin header)
curl -H "X-Autom9-Admin: localdev" \
     http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/test/google_docs
```

---

## 12. Adding a new env var

1. Open `app/core/config.py`
2. Add a field to the `Settings` class:
   ```python
   MY_NEW_VAR: str | None = None      # optional
   MY_REQUIRED_VAR: str = "default"   # with default
   ```
3. Add it to `autom9-backend/.env` and `autom9-backend/.env.example`
4. Access anywhere: `from app.core.config import settings` → `settings.MY_NEW_VAR`

---

## 13. Adding a new integration

Follow the same pattern as `google_docs.py`:

1. Create `app/integrations/my_service.py`
2. Inherit from `IntegrationBase`
3. Implement `name`, `health_check()`, `execute(action, params)`
4. Register in `app/integrations/__init__.py` → append to `ALL_INTEGRATIONS`
5. Create `tests/integrations/test_my_service.py` — mock `httpx.AsyncClient` to avoid real HTTP calls

Rules:
- `health_check()` **must never raise** — catch everything, return `status="unavailable"` on error
- `execute()` **raises `IntegrationError`** on failure — this becomes HTTP 503 at the API layer

---

## 14. Adding a new data endpoint

The `/api/data/` pattern (tasks, open-work) is the blueprint:

1. Add a schema to `app/schemas/data.py` (item model + response model)
2. Add a route to `app/api/data.py` — read config, call integration, return response model
3. Add or extend the integration action if needed (`execute("my_action", ...)`)
4. Add a test in `tests/api/test_data.py` — mock the integration's `execute()` method
5. Add a Svelte component in `autom9-extension/src/components/` and wire it up in `App.svelte`

---

## 15. Common commands cheat sheet

```bash
# Start the database
docker-compose up db

# Start the backend (auto-reload)
cd autom9-backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Start the frontend dev server
cd autom9-extension && npm run dev

# Run all tests
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest -v

# Run one test file
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py -v

# Run with coverage
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing

# Run migrations after pulling new changes
cd autom9-backend && uv run alembic upgrade head

# Generate a new encryption key
cd autom9-backend && uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```

---

## 16. When something goes wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `connection refused` on port 5432 | Postgres not running | `docker-compose up db` |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY not set` on startup | Missing `.env` | Copy `.env.example`, generate key |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Dependencies not installed | `uv sync` from `autom9-backend/` |
| `404` on `/api/data/open-work` | No active workflow config, or `open_work_board` not set | Configure via admin panel |
| `503` on any data endpoint | Integration credentials missing or Google token refresh failed | Check credentials in admin panel |
| Test fails with `IntegrationError` unexpectedly | Monkeypatch not setting all required credentials | Check `_configured()` or credential fields in the test |
| Alembic complains about head | New migration added | `uv run alembic upgrade head` |
| Frontend shows "Loading…" forever | Backend not running or CORS mismatch | Check `CORS_ORIGINS` in `.env` matches the dev server URL |

│   │   └── provider_factory.py ← Loads Anthropic or OpenAI provider
│   ├── config/               ← Workflow configuration system
│   │   └── workflow_schema.py ← Pydantic validation models for workflow JSON
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── config.py         ← All env vars (Settings class, read from .env)
│   │   └── exceptions.py     ← Custom exceptions (IntegrationError, etc.)
│   ├── db/                   ← Database layer
│   │   ├── engine.py         ← Async SQLAlchemy engine setup
│   │   └── dependencies.py   ← FastAPI get_db() dependency
│   ├── integrations/         ← External service clients
│   │   ├── base.py           ← Abstract interface every integration must implement
│   │   ├── google_calendar.py← Google Calendar (create invites)
│   │   ├── google_docs.py    ← Google Docs (fetch tasks, fetch open work)
│   │   ├── smartsheet.py     ← Smartsheet
│   │   └── __init__.py       ← ALL_INTEGRATIONS registry
│   ├── models/               ← SQLAlchemy ORM table definitions
│   ├── schemas/              ← Pydantic request/response shapes
│   │   ├── data.py           ← TaskItem, TasksResponse, OpportunityItem, OpenWorkResponse
│   │   └── status.py         ← Meta, StatusResponse
│   └── services/             ← Business logic helpers
│       └── encryption.py     ← Fernet-based credential encryption
└── tests/                    ← One file per app module
    ├── conftest.py           ← Fixtures: engine, db_session, client
    ├── agent/                ← Tests for provider implementations and masking
    ├── api/                  ← Tests for every API route
    │   ├── test_data.py      ← Tests for /api/data/tasks and /api/data/open-work
    │   └── test_open_work.py ← Additional open-work behaviour tests
    ├── config/               ← Tests for workflow config validation
    └── integrations/         ← Tests for each external service client

autom9-extension/src/
├── App.svelte                ← Root component: init, routing, shell
├── main.ts                   ← Vite entry point
├── app.css                   ← Global styles
├── components/
│   ├── DataPanel.svelte      ← Task list fetched from /api/data/tasks
│   ├── OpenWorkPanel.svelte  ← Opportunities fetched from /api/data/open-work
│   ├── ChatPanel.svelte      ← Chat interface
│   ├── StatusBar.svelte      ← Integration health badges
│   ├── AdminConfig.svelte    ← Admin panel (shown with ?admin query param)
│   ├── WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte ← Edit workflow JSON in-browser
│   ├── ActionConfirm.svelte  ← Tool-use confirmation dialog
│   ├── InputBar.svelte       ← Chat input field
│   └── MessageList.svelte    ← Chat history
├── lib/
│   ├── api.ts                ← Typed API client (all fetch calls go here)
│   └── tableau.ts            ← Tableau extension runtime shim
└── stores/
    ├── session.svelte.ts     ← Session ID, Tableau user ID
    ├── status.svelte.ts      ← Integration statuses
    ├── chat.svelte.ts        ← Chat messages and streaming state
    └── data.svelte.ts        ← Task and opportunity data
```

**Rule of thumb:** when you change `app/integrations/google_docs.py`, the test is `tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py`. Same pattern everywhere.

---

## 8. How a request travels end to end

Take **"load open work opportunities"** as a concrete example:

1. `OpenWorkPanel.svelte` mounts → calls `lib/api.ts` → `GET /api/data/open-work`
2. `app/api/data.py` handles the route:
   - reads `open_work_board.google_docs_url` from the active workflow config
   - calls `GoogleDocsIntegration().execute("fetch_open_work", {"url": ...})`
3. `app/integrations/google_docs.py`:
   - refreshes the OAuth2 access token (cached, thread-safe)
   - fetches the Google Doc via the Docs API
   - parses section headers (`Billable` / `Internal`) into structured items
4. Route handler maps the result to `OpenWorkResponse` (Pydantic schema in `app/schemas/data.py`)
5. JSON response returns → `OpenWorkPanel` renders badge + title for each item

To understand **any** feature, follow this same path: frontend component → `lib/api.ts` → backend route (`app/api/`) → integration or service → schema.

---

## 9. The workflow config system

Each "workflow" is a JSON blob stored in the database that tells the agent:
- What tools it can call (`tools` list)
- What instructions to follow (`agent_instructions`)
- Where to read task data (`data_panel.google_docs_url`)
- Where to read open work (`open_work_board.google_docs_url`)

`app/config/workflow_schema.py` validates this JSON using Pydantic. Key model:

```python
class WorkflowConfigSchema(BaseModel):
    version: str              # semver, e.g. "1.0.0"
    workflow_id: str          # unique identifier
    tools: list[ToolDefinition]
    agent_instructions: str
    data_panel: DataPanelConfig | None
    open_work_board: OpenWorkBoardConfig | None
```

Each `ToolDefinition` maps a tool name → integration name → action string, which is how the chat agent knows to call `GoogleCalendarIntegration.execute("create_invite", ...)` when the LLM invokes the `create_calendar_invite` tool.

You can edit the active workflow config at runtime through the `AdminConfig` panel (visible when the extension URL has `?admin` in it).

---

## 10. The integration system

All integrations implement the same three-method contract (`app/integrations/base.py`):

```python
class IntegrationBase(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str: ...         # e.g. "google_calendar"

    async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus: ...
    # NEVER raises — always returns status="healthy" or status="unavailable"

    async def execute(self, action: str, params: dict) -> dict: ...
    # Raises IntegrationError on failure — caught at the API layer → HTTP 503
```

Registered integrations (from `app/integrations/__init__.py`):

| Integration | `name` | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| `GoogleCalendarIntegration` | `google_calendar` | `create_invite` |
| `GoogleDocsIntegration` | `google_docs` | `fetch_tasks`, `fetch_open_work` |
| `SmartsheetIntegration` | `smartsheet` | (various) |
| `TableauDataIntegration` | `tableau` | (placeholder) |

---

## 11. Making a code change — end to end

### Step 1 — Find the file

| What you're changing | Where to look |
|---|---|
| API endpoint | `app/api/<name>.py` |
| Integration logic | `app/integrations/<name>.py` |
| Request/response shape | `app/schemas/<name>.py` |
| Env var | `app/core/config.py` → `Settings` class |
| Workflow config structure | `app/config/workflow_schema.py` |
| Frontend component | `autom9-extension/src/components/<Name>.svelte` |
| API calls from frontend | `autom9-extension/src/lib/api.ts` |

### Step 2 — Make the change

Edit the file. The server reloads automatically (if running with `--reload`).

### Step 3 — Run the relevant tests

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py -v
```

Test output shows exactly which assertion failed and on which line.

### Step 4 — Run the full suite

```bash
uv run pytest -v
```

If something outside your file breaks, you'll see it here.

### Step 5 — Manual smoke test (optional)

```bash
# Check all integration statuses
curl http://localhost:8000/api/status

# Fetch open-work data (requires active workflow config with open_work_board set)
curl http://localhost:8000/api/data/open-work

# Fetch task list
curl http://localhost:8000/api/data/tasks

# Test a specific integration (requires admin header)
curl -H "X-Autom9-Admin: localdev" \
     http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/test/google_docs
```

---

## 12. Adding a new env var

1. Open `app/core/config.py`
2. Add a field to the `Settings` class:
   ```python
   MY_NEW_VAR: str | None = None      # optional
   MY_REQUIRED_VAR: str = "default"   # with default
   ```
3. Add it to `autom9-backend/.env` and `autom9-backend/.env.example`
4. Access anywhere: `from app.core.config import settings` → `settings.MY_NEW_VAR`

---

## 13. Adding a new integration

Follow the same pattern as `google_docs.py`:

1. Create `app/integrations/my_service.py`
2. Inherit from `IntegrationBase`
3. Implement `name`, `health_check()`, `execute(action, params)`
4. Register in `app/integrations/__init__.py` → append to `ALL_INTEGRATIONS`
5. Create `tests/integrations/test_my_service.py` — mock `httpx.AsyncClient` to avoid real HTTP calls

Rules:
- `health_check()` **must never raise** — catch everything, return `status="unavailable"` on error
- `execute()` **raises `IntegrationError`** on failure — this becomes HTTP 503 at the API layer

---

## 14. Adding a new data endpoint

The `/api/data/` pattern (tasks, open-work) is the blueprint:

1. Add a schema to `app/schemas/data.py` (item model + response model)
2. Add a route to `app/api/data.py` — read config, call integration, return response model
3. Add or extend the integration action if needed (`execute("my_action", ...)`)
4. Add a test in `tests/api/test_data.py` — mock the integration's `execute()` method
5. Add a Svelte component in `autom9-extension/src/components/` and wire it up in `App.svelte`

---

## 15. Common commands cheat sheet

```bash
# Start the database
docker-compose up db

# Start the backend (auto-reload)
cd autom9-backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Start the frontend dev server
cd autom9-extension && npm run dev

# Run all tests
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest -v

# Run one test file
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py -v

# Run with coverage
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing

# Run migrations after pulling new changes
cd autom9-backend && uv run alembic upgrade head

# Generate a new encryption key
cd autom9-backend && uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```

---

## 16. When something goes wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `connection refused` on port 5432 | Postgres not running | `docker-compose up db` |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY not set` on startup | Missing `.env` | Copy `.env.example`, generate key |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Dependencies not installed | `uv sync` from `autom9-backend/` |
| `404` on `/api/data/open-work` | No active workflow config, or `open_work_board` not set | Configure via admin panel |
| `503` on any data endpoint | Integration credentials missing or Google token refresh failed | Check credentials in admin panel |
| Test fails with `IntegrationError` unexpectedly | Monkeypatch not setting all required credentials | Check `_configured()` or credential fields in the test |
| Alembic complains about head | New migration added | `uv run alembic upgrade head` |
| Frontend shows "Loading…" forever | Backend not running or CORS mismatch | Check `CORS_ORIGINS` in `.env` matches the dev server URL |

# Developer Walk-Me Guide
### How to run, test, and change autom9

This guide assumes you have Docker, Node.js, and `uv` installed but limited familiarity with the codebase. It covers everything from first boot to making and verifying a code change.

---

## 1. What the project is

autom9 is two things that work together:

| Part | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Backend** | A Python/FastAPI REST API | `autom9-backend/` |
| **Extension** | A Tableau extension (Svelte/TypeScript UI) | `autom9-extension/` |

The backend is what you'll spend most of your time on. It connects to a Postgres database, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools like Smartsheet and Google Calendar.

---

## 2. First-time setup

### 2a. Environment file

The backend needs secrets to start. Copy the example and fill in the two required values:

```bash
cp autom9-backend/.env.example autom9-backend/.env
```

Edit `autom9-backend/.env` — the only two lines that need real values for local dev:

```
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<any 32-byte base64 string>
BACKEND_SECRET=<any string you choose, e.g. "localdev">
```

To generate a valid `ENCRYPTION_KEY`:
```bash
uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
```
Run that from `autom9-backend/`. Paste the output into `.env`.

### 2b. Start the database

```bash
docker-compose up db
```

This starts a Postgres 16 container on port 5432. Leave it running in a terminal.

### 2c. Run database migrations

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

This creates all the tables. You only need to do this once (and again after any migration files are added).

---

## 3. Running the backend

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

`--reload` means the server restarts automatically when you save a Python file — you don't need to restart it manually after changes.

The API is now at `http://localhost:8000`. Check it's working:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

Interactive API docs (great for exploring endpoints):
```
http://localhost:8000/docs
```

---

## 4. Running the tests

All backend tests live in `autom9-backend/tests/`. **Tests do not need the backend server running** — they spin up their own in-memory app. They do need Postgres running (`docker-compose up db`).

### Run everything:
```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest -v
```

### Run a single test file:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
```

### Run a single test by name:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py::test_health_check_ok -v
```

### Run with coverage (see which lines are untested):
```bash
uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing
```

**Always use `uv run` prefix** — do not use `python`, `python3`, or bare `pytest`.

---

## 5. How the tests work

You don't need a real LLM key or real Google Calendar credentials to run tests. The tests use **mocks** — fake stand-ins that simulate the external services.

The test setup (`tests/conftest.py`) automatically:
- Generates a throwaway encryption key
- Points to a local test database (`autom9_test`)
- Creates all tables before tests and drops them after
- Wraps each test in a transaction that rolls back — so tests never leave dirty data

If a test uses the HTTP client, it goes through the real FastAPI app but with a fake database session injected. No real HTTP calls are made to Google, Smartsheet, etc. unless you explicitly write a test that does so.

---

## 6. Project layout (the parts you'll touch)

```
autom9-backend/
├── app/
│   ├── api/                  ← HTTP endpoints (routes, request handling)
│   │   ├── chat.py           ← The main chat + tool-confirmation flow
│   │   ├── integrations.py   ← Health check endpoints
│   │   └── admin/            ← Admin routes (credentials, config, logs)
│   ├── integrations/         ← External service clients
│   │   ├── base.py           ← Interface every integration must implement
│   │   ├── google_calendar.py← Google Calendar (story 3.6)
│   │   ├── smartsheet.py     ← Smartsheet (story 3.5)
│   │   └── __init__.py       ← Registry of all integrations
│   ├── agent/
│   │   ├── masking.py        ← PII token masking / rehydration
│   │   └── provider_factory.py← LLM provider loader
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── config.py         ← All env vars live here (Settings class)
│   │   └── exceptions.py     ← Custom exceptions (IntegrationError, etc.)
│   ├── models/               ← Database table definitions (SQLAlchemy)
│   └── schemas/              ← Request/response shapes (Pydantic)
└── tests/                    ← Mirror of app/ — one test file per module
```

**Rule of thumb:** when you change a file in `app/integrations/`, the corresponding test is in `tests/integrations/`. Same pattern everywhere.

---

## 7. Making a code change — end to end

Here's the full loop for a typical change.

### Step 1 — Find the file

If you're changing how Google Calendar works: `app/integrations/google_calendar.py`.  
If you're adding an env var: `app/core/config.py` (add it to the `Settings` class).  
If you're changing an API endpoint: `app/api/<relevant_file>.py`.

### Step 2 — Make the change

Edit the file. The server reloads automatically (if it's running with `--reload`).

### Step 3 — Run the relevant tests

```bash
cd autom9-backend
uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v
```

If tests fail, the output will show you exactly which assertion failed and on which line.

### Step 4 — Run the full suite

```bash
uv run pytest -v
```

207 tests should pass. If something outside your file broke, you'll see it here.

### Step 5 — Manual smoke test (optional)

With the server running (`uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload`), you can hit the API directly:

```bash
# Check all integration health statuses
curl http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/status

# Check a specific integration (requires admin header)
curl -H "X-Autom9-Admin: <your BACKEND_SECRET>" \
     http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/test/google_calendar
```

---

## 8. Adding a new env var

1. Open `app/core/config.py`
2. Add a field to the `Settings` class:
   ```python
   MY_NEW_VAR: str | None = None      # optional
   MY_REQUIRED_VAR: str = "default"   # with default
   ```
3. Add it to `autom9-backend/.env` (and `.env.example`)
4. Access it anywhere in the app: `from app.core.config import settings` then `settings.MY_NEW_VAR`

---

## 9. Adding a new integration

All integrations follow the same pattern as `google_calendar.py`:

1. Create `app/integrations/my_service.py`
2. Inherit from `IntegrationBase` (defined in `app/integrations/base.py`)
3. Implement `name`, `health_check()`, and `execute(action, params)`
4. Register it in `app/integrations/__init__.py` by adding it to `ALL_INTEGRATIONS`
5. Create `tests/integrations/test_my_service.py` — mock `httpx.AsyncClient` to avoid real HTTP calls

The `health_check()` method **must never raise** — always return an `IntegrationStatus`. The `execute()` method raises `IntegrationError` on failure.

---

## 10. Common commands cheat sheet

```bash
# Start the database
docker-compose up db

# Start the backend server (auto-reloads on change)
cd autom9-backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Run all tests
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest -v

# Run one test file
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v

# Run migrations after pulling new changes
cd autom9-backend && uv run alembic upgrade head

# Generate a new encryption key
cd autom9-backend && uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"

# Check test coverage for a module
cd autom9-backend && uv run pytest --cov=app/integrations --cov-report=term-missing
```

---

## 11. When something goes wrong

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `connection refused` on port 5432 | Postgres not running | `docker-compose up db` |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY not set` on startup | Missing `.env` | Copy `.env.example`, generate key |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Dependencies not installed | `uv sync` from `autom9-backend/` |
| Test fails with `IntegrationError` unexpectedly | Monkeypatch not setting all credentials | Check `_configured()` helper in the test |
| Alembic complains about head | New migration added by someone else | `uv run alembic upgrade head` |

# Create Story Workflow

**Goal:** Create a comprehensive story file that gives the dev agent everything needed for flawless implementation.

**Your Role:** Story context engine that prevents LLM developer mistakes, omissions, or disasters.
- Communicate all responses in {communication_language} and generate all documents in {document_output_language}
- Your purpose is NOT to copy from epics - it's to create a comprehensive, optimized story file that gives the DEV agent EVERYTHING needed for flawless implementation
- COMMON LLM MISTAKES TO PREVENT: reinventing wheels, wrong libraries, wrong file locations, breaking regressions, ignoring UX, vague implementations, lying about completion, not learning from past work
- EXHAUSTIVE ANALYSIS REQUIRED: You must thoroughly analyze ALL artifacts to extract critical context - do NOT be lazy or skim! This is the most important function in the entire development process!
- UTILIZE SUBPROCESSES AND SUBAGENTS: Use research subagents, subprocesses or parallel processing if available to thoroughly analyze different artifacts simultaneously and thoroughly
- SAVE QUESTIONS: If you think of questions or clarifications during analysis, save them for the end after the complete story is written
- ZERO USER INTERVENTION: Process should be fully automated except for initial epic/story selection or missing documents

---

## INITIALIZATION

### Configuration Loading

Load config from `{project-root}/_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` and resolve:

- `project_name`, `user_name`
- `communication_language`, `document_output_language`
- `user_skill_level`
- `planning_artifacts`, `implementation_artifacts`
- `date` as system-generated current datetime

### Paths

- `sprint_status` = `{implementation_artifacts}/sprint-status.yaml`
- `epics_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/epics.md`
- `prd_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/prd.md`
- `architecture_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/architecture.md`
- `ux_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*.md`
- `story_title` = "" (will be elicited if not derivable)
- `project_context` = `**/project-context.md` (load if exists)
- `default_output_file` = `{implementation_artifacts}/{{story_key}}.md`

### Input Files

| Input | Description | Path Pattern(s) | Load Strategy |
|-------|-------------|------------------|---------------|
| prd | PRD (fallback - epics file should have most content) | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |
| architecture | Architecture (fallback - epics file should have relevant sections) | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |
| ux | UX design (fallback - epics file should have relevant sections) | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |
| epics | Enhanced epics+stories file with BDD and source hints | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*epic*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*epic*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |

---

## EXECUTION

<workflow>

<step n="1" goal="Determine target story">
  <check if="{{story_path}} is provided by user or user provided the epic and story number such as 2-4 or 1.6 or epic 1 story 5">

    <action>Set {{epic_num}}, {{story_num}}, {{story_key}} from user input</action>
    <action>GOTO step 2a</action>
  </check>

  <action>Check if {{sprint_status}} file exists for auto discover</action>
  <check if="sprint status file does NOT exist">
    <output>🚫 No sprint status file found and no story specified</output>
    <output>
      **Required Options:**
      1. Run `sprint-planning` to initialize sprint tracking (recommended)
      2. Provide specific epic-story number to create (e.g., "1-2-user-auth")
      3. Provide path to story documents if sprint status doesn't exist yet
    </output>
    <ask>Choose option [1], provide epic-story number, path to story docs, or [q] to quit:</ask>

    <check if="user chooses 'q'">
      <action>HALT - No work needed</action>
    </check>

    <check if="user chooses '1'">
      <output>Run sprint-planning workflow first to create sprint-status.yaml</output>
      <action>HALT - User needs to run sprint-planning</action>

    </check>

      <action>GOTO step 2a</action>

        <output>2. Create a new epic for additional work</output>

        <action>HALT - Cannot proceed</action>
      </check>
      <output>📊 Epic {{epic_num}} status updated to in-progress</output>
    </check>

  </check>
  <action>Load the FULL file: {{sprint_status}}</action>
  <action>Read ALL lines from beginning to end - do not skip any content</action>

    - story_num: second number after first dash (e.g., "2")
    - story_title: remainder after second dash (e.g., "user-authentication")
  </action>
  <action>Set {{story_id}} = "{{epic_num}}.{{story_num}}"</action>
  <action>Store story_key for later use (e.g., "1-2-user-authentication")</action>

  <!-- Mark epic as in-progress if this is first story -->
  <action>Check if this is the first story in epic {{epic_num}} by looking for {{epic_num}}-1-* pattern</action>
  <check if="this is first story in epic {{epic_num}}">
    <action>Load {{sprint_status}} and check epic-{{epic_num}} status</action>
    <action>If epic status is "backlog" → update to "in-progress"</action>

1	# Discover Inputs Protocol
2	
3	**Objective:** Intelligently load project files (whole or sharded) based on the workflow's Input Files configuration.
4	
5	**Prerequisite:** Only execute this protocol if the workflow defines an Input Files section. If no input file patterns are configured, skip this entirely.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Step 1: Parse Input File Patterns
10	
11	- Read the Input Files table from the workflow configuration.
12	- For each input group (prd, architecture, epics, ux, etc.), note the **load strategy** if specified.
13	
14	## Step 2: Load Files Using Smart Strategies
15	
16	For each pattern in the Input Files table, work through the following substeps in order:
17	
18	### 2a: Try Sharded Documents First
19	
20	If a sharded pattern exists for this input, determine the load strategy (defaults to **FULL_LOAD** if not specified), then apply the matching strategy:
21	
22	#### FULL_LOAD Strategy
23	
24	Load ALL files in the sharded directory. Use this for PRD, Architecture, UX, brownfield docs, or whenever the full picture is needed.
25	
26	1. Use the glob pattern to find ALL `.md` files (e.g., `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*/*.md`).
27	2. Load EVERY matching file completely.
28	3. Concatenate content in logical order: `index.md` first if it exists, then alphabetical.
29	4. Store the combined result in a variable named `{pattern_name_content}` (e.g., `{architecture_content}`).
30	
31	#### SELECTIVE_LOAD Strategy
32	
33	Load a specific shard using a template variable. Example: used for epics with `{{epic_num}}`.
34	
35	1. Check for template variables in the sharded pattern (e.g., `{{epic_num}}`).
36	2. If the variable is undefined, ask the user for the value OR infer it from context.
37	3. Resolve the template to a specific file path.
38	4. Load that specific file.
39	5. Store in variable: `{pattern_name_content}`.
40	
41	#### INDEX_GUIDED Strategy
42	
43	Load index.md, analyze the structure and description of each doc in the index, then intelligently load relevant docs.
44	
45	**DO NOT BE LAZY** -- use best judgment to load documents that might have relevant information, even if there is only a 5% chance of relevance.
46	
47	1. Load `index.md` from the sharded directory.
48	2. Parse the table of contents, links, and section headers.
49	3. Analyze the workflow's purpose and objective.
50	4. Identify which linked/referenced documents are likely relevant.
51	   - *Example:* If the workflow is about authentication and the index shows "Auth Overview", "Payment Setup", "Deployment" -- load the auth docs, consider deployment docs, skip payment.
52	5. Load all identified relevant documents.
53	6. Store combined content in variable: `{pattern_name_content}`.
54	
55	**When in doubt, LOAD IT** -- context is valuable, and being thorough is better than missing critical info.
56	
57	---
58	
59	After applying the matching strategy, mark the pattern as **RESOLVED** and move to the next pattern.
60	
61	### 2b: Try Whole Document if No Sharded Found
62	
63	If no sharded matches were found OR no sharded pattern exists for this input:
64	
65	1. Attempt a glob match on the "whole" pattern (e.g., `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*.md`).
66	2. If matches are found, load ALL matching files completely (no offset/limit).
67	3. Store content in variable: `{pattern_name_content}` (e.g., `{prd_content}`).
68	4. Mark pattern as **RESOLVED** and move to the next pattern.
69	
70	### 2c: Handle Not Found
71	
72	If no matches were found for either sharded or whole patterns:
73	
74	1. Set `{pattern_name_content}` to empty string.
75	2. Note in session: "No {pattern_name} files found" -- this is not an error, just unavailable. Offer the user a chance to provide the file.
76	
77	## Step 3: Report Discovery Results
78	
79	List all loaded content variables with file counts. Example:
80	
81	```
82	OK Loaded {prd_content} from 5 sharded files: prd/index.md, prd/requirements.md, ...
83	OK Loaded {architecture_content} from 1 file: Architecture.md
84	OK Loaded {epics_content} from selective load: epics/epic-3.md
85	-- No ux_design files found
86	```
87	
88	This gives the workflow transparency into what context is available.

2. If the variable is undefined, ask the user for the value OR infer it from context.
3. Resolve the template to a specific file path.
4. Load that specific file.
5. Store in variable: `{pattern_name_content}`.

#### INDEX_GUIDED Strategy

Load index.md, analyze the structure and description of each doc in the index, then intelligently load relevant docs.

**DO NOT BE LAZY** -- use best judgment to load documents that might have relevant information, even if there is only a 5% chance of relevance.

1. Load `index.md` from the sharded directory.
2. Parse the table of contents, links, and section headers.
3. Analyze the workflow's purpose and objective.
4. Identify which linked/referenced documents are likely relevant.
   - *Example:* If the workflow is about authentication and the index shows "Auth Overview", "Payment Setup", "Deployment" -- load the auth docs, consider deployment docs, skip payment.
5. Load all identified relevant documents.
6. Store combined content in variable: `{pattern_name_content}`.

**When in doubt, LOAD IT** -- context is valuable, and being thorough is better than missing critical info.

---

After applying the matching strategy, mark the pattern as **RESOLVED** and move to the next pattern.

### 2b: Try Whole Document if No Sharded Found

If no sharded matches were found OR no sharded pattern exists for this input:

1. Attempt a glob match on the "whole" pattern (e.g., `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*.md`).
2. If matches are found, load ALL matching files completely (no offset/limit).
3. Store content in variable: `{pattern_name_content}` (e.g., `{prd_content}`).
4. Mark pattern as **RESOLVED** and move to the next pattern.

### 2c: Handle Not Found

If no matches were found for either sharded or whole patterns:

1. Set `{pattern_name_content}` to empty string.
2. Note in session: "No {pattern_name} files found" -- this is not an error, just unavailable. Offer the user a chance to provide the file.

## Step 3: Report Discovery Results

List all loaded content variables with file counts. Example:

```
OK Loaded {prd_content} from 5 sharded files: prd/index.md, prd/requirements.md, ...
OK Loaded {architecture_content} from 1 file: Architecture.md
OK Loaded {epics_content} from selective load: epics/epic-3.md
-- No ux_design files found
```

This gives the workflow transparency into what context is available.

6	# autom9 - Epic Breakdown
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for autom9, decomposing the requirements from the PRD and Architecture into implementable stories.
11	
12	## Requirements Inventory
13	
14	### Functional Requirements
15	
16	FR1: Consultant can view their open days and scheduled engagements sourced from Snowflake via the Tableau data source within the extension panel
17	FR2: Consultant can view their task list ingested from their designated individual Google Doc
18	FR3: Consultant can interact with the AI agent via a chat interface embedded in the Tableau extension panel
19	FR4: Agent can ask clarifying questions about task timing, priority, and scheduling preferences before taking action
20	FR5: Agent retains context within a session to support multi-turn clarifying conversations
21	FR6: Consultant can review the agent's proposed actions before execution is confirmed
22	FR7: Agent surfaces open work opportunities from the org-wide Google Doc, distinguishing billable client work from internal projects
23	FR8: Agent prioritises billable opportunities above internal project opportunities
24	FR9: Agent calculates whether a consultant's available capacity meets the time commitment of an open work opportunity, including a 5% buffer
25	FR10: Consultant can accept or decline an open work opportunity from within the extension panel
26	FR11: Agent notifies the relevant coordinator when a consultant accepts an open work opportunity
27	FR12: Agent does not resurface a previously declined opportunity to the same consultant
28	FR13: Agent submits a Smartsheet planning request on behalf of the consultant
29	FR14: Agent creates Google Calendar invites for the consultant around existing engagements
30	FR15: Extension checks connectivity to all configured integrations on load and surfaces any unavailable services before interaction begins
31	FR16: Agent fails gracefully with a specific error message if an integration becomes unavailable during a workflow, without partially executing dependent actions
32	FR17: Agent masks identifiable data fields (names, client identifiers, engagement IDs) with opaque tokens before transmitting any context to the LLM provider
33	FR18: Agent rehydrates masked tokens with real values from the session token map before displaying output or executing tool actions
34	FR19: Integration credentials are never exposed in logs, the chat interface, or configuration files visible to consultants
35	FR20: Admin can install and register the extension in Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server
36	FR21: Admin can configure the BYOM LLM provider and API credentials at the org level via the extension configuration panel
37	FR22: Admin can load and update the JSON workflow configuration file defining agent capabilities, tool access, and workflow parameters
38	FR23: Admin can test integration connections from the configuration panel before activating the extension for consultants
39	FR24: Admin can access agent interaction logs with sufficient detail to diagnose failed tool calls, error patterns, and latency
40	FR25: Integration status check results are logged for admin review
41	FR26: New agent workflows can be added by updating the JSON workflow configuration file without modifying platform code
42	FR27: The JSON workflow configuration defines available tools, agent instructions, and workflow parameters in a versionable format
43	FR28: The extension supports OpenAI and Anthropic as BYOM LLM providers, switchable via configuration change
44	FR29: The extension is compatible with Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server
45	
46	### NonFunctional Requirements
47	
48	NFR1: Agent responses complete within 20 seconds (p95) under normal operating conditions during the POC phase (nice-to-have; no hard SLA in v1)
49	NFR2: The extension panel renders and integration status check completes within 5 seconds of Tableau dashboard load
50	NFR3: The chat interface displays a visible processing indicator within 1 second of the consultant submitting a message
51	NFR4: All data transmitted between the extension and external services is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+)
52	NFR5: API credentials and integration tokens are stored encrypted at rest and never surfaced in logs, UI elements, or configuration files accessible to consultants
53	NFR6: The token masking system transmits no real consultant names, client identifiers, or engagement IDs to any external LLM provider under any circumstances
54	NFR7: Agent interaction logs capture only masked data representations — no raw LLM payloads containing identifiable fields
55	NFR8: The extension identifies and reports unavailability of any configured integration within the 5-second load status check window
56	NFR9: A failure in one integration does not cascade to prevent other integrations from functioning
57	NFR10: The JSON workflow configuration system handles version mismatches gracefully — a config update does not break or corrupt an in-flight session
58	NFR11: The extension supports concurrent usage by all 80 POC consultants without degradation in agent response time
59	NFR12: The platform architecture imposes no design constraints that would prevent future multi-tenant isolation
60	
61	### Additional Requirements
62	
63	- **[ARC-1] Project Scaffolding (Day-Zero):** Backend scaffold: `uv init autom9-backend` with fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy[asyncio], asyncpg, alembic, pydantic-settings, python-jose, httpx, cryptography, python-json-logger. Frontend scaffold: `npm create vite@latest autom9-extension -- --template svelte-ts` with @tableau/extensions-api-types.
64	- **[ARC-2] .trex Manifest:** Create `autom9.trex` at extension project root with required fields: name, description, source-location (backend URL), min-version, permissions (read worksheets). Without this the extension cannot load for any testing.
65	- **[ARC-3] CORS Configuration:** Configure FastAPI `CORSMiddleware` in `main.py` with allowed Tableau origins (public.tableau.com and Tableau Server domain).
66	- **[ARC-4] JSON Workflow Config Schema:** Document schema in `app/config/workflow_schema.py` — minimum fields: version (semver), tools (array with name, description, parameters), agent_instructions (string), workflow_id (string).
67	- **[ARC-5] Tableau initializeAsync Gate:** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` must complete before any store setup or backend calls in `App.svelte`.
68	- **[ARC-6] Alembic Fail-Fast:** Container must fail to start if migration fails. Enforced via Docker entrypoint exit code check.
69	- **[ARC-7] Async Test Setup:** `pytest.ini` must specify `asyncio_mode = auto`. Async SQLAlchemy fixtures must be function-scoped to prevent state leakage.
70	- **[ARC-8] Connection Pool Sizing:** `DATABASE_POOL_MIN` and `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` as environment variables (recommended: min=5, max=20) via pydantic-settings.
71	- **[ARC-9] masking.py Quality Gate:** `app/agent/masking.py` requires 100% branch coverage as a hard acceptance criterion for any story touching the agent pipeline.
72	- **[ARC-10] LLM Retry/Backoff Strategy:** `LLMProvider.complete()` must apply exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries max, then raise `ProviderError` on 429 or transient errors.
73	- **[ARC-11] Data Models:** Four core models required: `DeclinedOpportunity` (consultant_id, opportunity_id, declined_at), `InteractionLog` (session_id, masked_input, masked_output, tool_calls, latency_ms, timestamp), `CredentialStore` (org_id, provider, encrypted_key), `WorkflowConfig` (version, config_json, loaded_at), `Session` (session_id UUID PK, tableau_user_id, started_at).
74	- **[ARC-12] BYOM Provider Interface:** `LLMProvider` class with `complete()` and `stream()` — stream() raises `NotImplementedError` in v1.
75	- **[ARC-13] Integration Interface:** All integrations in `app/integrations/` implement `IntegrationBase` with `health_check()` and `execute()`. Failure raises `IntegrationError` caught at `app/api/` level.
76	- **[ARC-14] Session Registry:** `GET /api/admin/sessions/{session_id}` endpoint for admin triage. All `InteractionLog` entries reference session_id. PII stays out of logs.
77	
78	### UX Design Requirements
79	
80	No UX design document present for this project.
81	
82	### FR Coverage Map
83	
84	FR1:  Epic 3 — Tableau/Snowflake data panel
85	FR2:  Epic 3 — Individual Google Docs task list ingestion
86	FR3:  Epic 3 — Chat interface in extension panel
87	FR4:  Epic 3 — Agent clarifying Q&A before action
88	FR5:  Epic 3 — Multi-turn session context retention
89	FR6:  Epic 3 — Action confirmation before execution
90	FR7:  Epic 4 — Org-wide Google Doc open work surfacing
91	FR8:  Epic 4 — Billable > internal prioritisation
92	FR9:  Epic 4 — Capacity + 5% buffer calculation
93	FR10: Epic 4 — Accept/decline flow in panel
94	FR11: Epic 4 — Coordinator notification on accept
95	FR12: Epic 4 — Declined opportunity persistence
96	FR13: Epic 3 — Smartsheet planning request
97	FR14: Epic 3 — Google Calendar invite creation
98	FR15: Epic 1 — Integration health check on load
99	FR16: Epic 1 — Graceful failure isolation (pattern); Epic 3 (agent pipeline enforcement)
100	FR17: Epic 3 — Token masking before LLM calls
101	FR18: Epic 3 — Token rehydration before output/actions
102	FR19: Epic 2 — Credentials never in logs/UI/config
103	FR20: Epic 2 — Extension install (Desktop + Cloud)
104	FR21: Epic 2 — BYOM credential configuration (org-level)
105	FR22: Epic 2 — JSON workflow config load/update
106	FR23: Epic 2 — Integration connection testing from admin panel
107	FR24: Epic 2 — Admin interaction log access
108	FR25: Epic 2 — Status check results logged
109	FR26: Epic 2 — New workflows via JSON config, no code changes
110	FR27: Epic 2 — JSON config defines tools, instructions, params (versionable)
111	FR28: Epic 2 — OpenAI + Anthropic BYOM switching via config
112	FR29: Epic 1 — Tableau Desktop + Cloud/Server compatibility
113	
114	## Epic List
115	
116	### Epic 1: Platform Foundation & Extension Shell
117	
118	The extension loads in Tableau, renders a status panel, and confirms that all configured integrations are reachable — giving consultants and admins a trustworthy starting point for every session.
119	
120	**FRs covered:** FR15, FR16 (isolation pattern established), FR29
121	**ARCs covered:** ARC-1, ARC-2, ARC-3, ARC-5, ARC-6, ARC-7, ARC-8, ARC-11 (Session, CredentialStore, WorkflowConfig, InteractionLog only), ARC-12 (interface only), ARC-13 (interface only), ARC-14
122	**NFRs covered:** NFR2, NFR4, NFR8, NFR9, NFR12
123	
124	> Note: `DeclinedOpportunity` model deferred to Epic 4 (migration-first — no schema for features not yet built).

127	
128	An admin can fully configure the extension — set BYOM credentials, load a JSON workflow config, test all integrations, and review interaction logs — making the extension ready for consultants to use.
129	
130	**FRs covered:** FR19, FR20, FR21, FR22, FR23, FR24, FR25, FR26, FR27, FR28
131	**ARCs covered:** ARC-4, ARC-9 (quality gate policy defined), ARC-10 (LLM retry/backoff), ARC-12 (concrete OpenAI + Anthropic implementations), ARC-13 (concrete integration implementations)
132	**NFRs covered:** NFR5, NFR10
133	
134	### Epic 3: Consultant Planning Request Workflow (Core POC)
135	
136	A consultant can open the extension, see their open days and task list, have a multi-turn clarifying conversation with the agent, and complete a Smartsheet planning request with Google Calendar invites — without leaving Tableau.
137	
138	**FRs covered:** FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, FR5, FR6, FR13, FR14, FR16 (enforced in pipeline), FR17, FR18

143
