150	---
151	
152	## Epic 1: Platform Foundation & Extension Shell
153	
154	Both the backend server and Tableau extension frontend are scaffolded, the extension loads inside Tableau without errors, and a parallel integration health check runs on load — giving consultants and admins a trustworthy, observable starting point before any agent interaction begins.
155	
156	### Story 1.1: Project Scaffolding & Backend Foundation
157	
158	As an **admin/developer**,
159	I want both the backend server and extension frontend scaffolded with all foundational tooling configured,
160	So that the development team has a runnable, tested baseline to build every subsequent story on.
161	
162	**Acceptance Criteria:**
163	
164	**Given** the repository is freshly cloned
165	**When** `docker compose up` is run
166	**Then** the backend API container starts successfully and `GET /health` returns `{"status": "ok"}`
167	**And** the PostgreSQL container starts and Alembic migrations run to completion (tables: `sessions`, `interaction_logs`, `credential_store`, `workflow_configs`)
168	**And** if migrations fail, the container exits with a non-zero code (fail-fast enforced)
169	
170	**Given** the frontend scaffold exists
171	**When** `npm run dev` is run
172	**Then** the Vite dev server starts and serves the extension shell on localhost
173	
174	**Given** `pytest` is run against the backend
175	**When** tests execute
176	**Then** `asyncio_mode = auto` is active, all fixtures are function-scoped, and the test suite passes with zero failures
177	
178	**Given** the pydantic-settings config is loaded
179	**When** the app starts
180	**Then** `DATABASE_URL`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `BACKEND_SECRET`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `DATABASE_POOL_MIN`, `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` are all resolved from environment variables and the app fails to start if any required variable is missing
181	
182	**Dev notes:** ARC-1, ARC-6, ARC-7, ARC-8, ARC-11 (schema only — no application logic yet)
183	
184	---
185	
186	### Story 1.2: Tableau Extension Shell & Initialization
187	
188	As an **admin**,
189	I want the autom9 extension to load inside a Tableau dashboard without errors,
190	So that consultants see the extension panel and the system is ready to make backend calls.
191	
192	**Acceptance Criteria:**
193	
194	**Given** the `.trex` manifest is registered in Tableau Desktop or Tableau Cloud
195	**When** a consultant opens a Tableau dashboard with the autom9 extension
196	**Then** the extension panel renders without a blank screen or error message
197	
198	**Given** the extension panel has mounted
199	**When** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` is called
200	**Then** no store initialization or backend HTTP calls begin until the promise resolves
201	**And** if `initializeAsync()` rejects, the extension displays a clear load-failure message
202	
203	**Given** the extension is running in development
204	**When** the extension frontend makes an HTTP call to the backend
205	**Then** CORS headers are accepted for the configured Tableau origins (no CORS errors in browser console)
206	
207	**Given** any Tableau Dashboard (Desktop or Cloud/Server)
208	**When** the extension is loaded
209	**Then** the extension shell renders correctly in both environments (FR29)

250	## Epic 2: Admin Configuration & Extension Management
251	
252	An admin can fully configure the extension — set BYOM credentials, load a JSON workflow config, test all integrations, and review interaction logs — making the extension ready for consultants to use.

254	### Story 2.1: Admin Config Panel & BYOM Credential Setup
255	
256	As an **admin**,
257	I want to configure the BYOM LLM provider and API credentials from the extension's admin panel,

259	
260	**Acceptance Criteria:**
261	
262	**Given** the extension is loaded and the admin opens the config panel
263	**When** `AdminConfig.svelte` renders
264	**Then** the panel displays fields for LLM provider selection (OpenAI / Anthropic) and API key input (FR20, FR21)

266	**Given** an admin submits valid BYOM credentials via `POST /api/admin/credentials`
267	**When** the backend processes the request
268	**Then** the API key is encrypted using Fernet symmetric encryption before storage in `credential_store`
269	**And** the plaintext key is never written to logs, response bodies, or any database column (FR19, NFR5)
270	
271	**Given** credentials are stored
272	**When** the admin revisits the config panel
273	**Then** the key field displays a masked placeholder (e.g., `••••••••`) — the raw value is never returned by any API endpoint (NFR5)

275	**Given** invalid or missing credentials are submitted
276	**When** `POST /api/admin/credentials` is called
277	**Then** the API returns a `400` with a structured error — no stack trace or internal detail exposed

283	### Story 2.2: JSON Workflow Configuration System
284	
285	As an **admin**,
286	I want to upload and update a JSON workflow configuration file that defines the agent's available tools and instructions,

290	
291	**Given** a valid JSON workflow config is uploaded via `POST /api/admin/config`
292	**When** `WorkflowRegistry` processes the file

294	**And** the config is stored in `workflow_configs` with `version`, `config_json`, and `loaded_at`

296	**Given** the extension loads
297	**When** `GET /api/config/workflow` is called
298	**Then** the current active workflow config is returned and `WorkflowRegistry.get_tool_definitions()` reflects the loaded tools (FR22, FR27)
299	
300	**Given** a new config is uploaded while a session is in progress

302	**Then** the session continues using the config version it started with — no disruption or corruption (NFR10)
303	
304	**Given** an invalid or version-mismatched config is uploaded
305	**When** `validate_schema()` runs
306	**Then** the upload is rejected with a clear error and the previous active config remains unchanged (FR26, FR27)

312	### Story 2.3: BYOM Provider Implementations
313	
314	As an **admin**,
315	I want to switch the active LLM provider between OpenAI and Anthropic via configuration,

318	**Acceptance Criteria:**
319	
320	**Given** OpenAI is set as the active BYOM provider in credentials

322	**Then** `OpenAIProvider.complete()` is invoked with the correct message format for the OpenAI API

324	**Given** Anthropic is set as the active BYOM provider
325	**When** the agent makes an LLM call

332	
333	**Given** `LLMProvider.stream()` is called
334	**When** the method executes
335	**Then** it raises `NotImplementedError` (streaming deferred to v2; interface is set)
336	
337	**Given** the provider is switched from OpenAI to Anthropic via a config change

340	
341	**Dev notes:** ARC-10, ARC-12 (concrete implementations), FR28

345	### Story 2.4: Integration Connection Testing
346	
347	As an **admin**,
348	I want to test each integration connection from the config panel before activating the extension for consultants,

375	### Story 2.5: Admin Interaction Log Access
376	
377	As an **admin**,

405	## Epic 3: Consultant Planning Request Workflow (Core POC)
406	
407	A consultant can open the extension, see their open days and task list, have a multi-turn clarifying conversation with the agent, and complete a Smartsheet planning request with Google Calendar invites — without leaving Tableau.
408	
409	### Story 3.1: Planning Data Display Panel
410	
411	As a **consultant**,
412	I want to see my open days and task list inside the extension panel,
413	So that I have the context I need before starting a planning conversation with the agent.
414	
415	**Acceptance Criteria:**
416	
417	**Given** the extension has initialized and the consultant's Tableau session is active
418	**When** `DataPanel.svelte` loads
419	**Then** the consultant's open days and scheduled engagements are displayed, sourced from the Tableau worksheet data via `tableau.ts` (FR1)

422	**When** the panel loads

426	**When** `DataPanel.svelte` loads
427	**Then** it reads that worksheet via `tableau.ts` using the configured name — not a hardcoded worksheet identifier
428	**And** `DataPanel.svelte` renders the returned data generically — layout is not wired to planning-specific field names

430	**Given** the Snowflake/Tableau data source is unavailable
431	**When** the data panel attempts to load

434	**Given** the Google Docs integration is unavailable

442	### Story 3.2: Token Masking & Rehydration Pipeline
443	
444	As a **consultant**,
445	I want my personal and client data to be protected from exposure to external LLM providers,

448	**Acceptance Criteria:**
449	
450	**Given** consultant data (names, client identifiers, engagement IDs) enters `app/agent/`
451	**When** `masking.py` processes the data
452	**Then** all identifiable fields are replaced with opaque tokens (e.g. `CONSULTANT_X`, `CLIENT_A`, `ENGAGEMENT_001`) before any LLM call is made (FR17, NFR6)
453	
454	**Given** a session token map is initialised
455	**When** the extension loads (session start)
456	**Then** `sessionStore` holds an empty `Map<string, string>` — never populated from `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`
457	**And** the token map resets to empty on every extension load

459	**Given** the LLM returns a response containing masked tokens
460	**When** `masking.py` rehydrates the response
461	**Then** all opaque tokens are replaced with their real values from the session token map before output is displayed or tool actions are executed (FR18)
462	
463	**Given** a log entry is written after an LLM call
464	**When** the masking filter applies
465	**Then** the log contains `masked_input` and `masked_output` only — no raw consultant names, client names, or engagement IDs appear anywhere in the log (NFR7)

471	**Dev notes:** FR17, FR18, NFR6, NFR7, ARC-9 — `app/agent/masking.py` as a pipeline step; never inline in orchestration logic

475	### Story 3.3: Agent Chat Interface
476	
477	As a **consultant**,
478	I want to type messages to the agent and see responses in a chat panel,

511	### Story 3.4: Agent Orchestration & Action Confirmation
512	
513	As a **consultant**,
514	I want the agent to ask clarifying questions before taking action and show me what it's about to do before executing,

516	
517	**Acceptance Criteria:**
518	
519	**Given** a consultant sends a planning-related message
520	**When** the agent determines clarification is needed (e.g. flexible timing, urgent deliverable)
521	**Then** the agent responds with specific clarifying questions before dispatching any tool call (FR4)
522	
523	**Given** the agent has gathered sufficient context and is ready to act
524	**When** it prepares a tool call
525	**Then** `ActionConfirm.svelte` renders showing the proposed action before execution (FR6)
526	
527	**Given** the consultant confirms the proposed action
528	**When** `ActionConfirm.svelte` fires the confirmation
529	**Then** the tool call is dispatched and execution proceeds
530	
531	**Given** the consultant dismisses the confirmation
532	**When** the action is cancelled
533	**Then** the agent acknowledges the cancellation and returns to idle — no partial tool execution occurs (FR16)
534	
535	**Given** an integration becomes unavailable mid-workflow after confirmation
536	**When** the tool call attempts to execute
537	**Then** the agent fails with a specific plain-language error message and does not execute any dependent subsequent actions (FR16)
538	
539	**Given** the agent receives a tool call name from the LLM response
540	**When** it dispatches the tool
541	**Then** it resolves the implementation via `WorkflowRegistry.get_tool_definitions()` by tool name — no hardcoded `if tool == "smartsheet"` or `if tool == "google_calendar"` logic exists in the orchestration layer
542	**And** a future use case adding a new tool requires only a new `IntegrationBase` implementation and a JSON config update — zero changes to the orchestration layer

552	### Story 3.5: Smartsheet Planning Request Integration
553	
554	As a **consultant**,
555	I want the agent to submit a Smartsheet planning request on my behalf,

558	**Acceptance Criteria:**
559	
560	**Given** the consultant has confirmed a planning action and the orchestration layer dispatches the registered Smartsheet tool
561	**When** `SmartsheetIntegration.execute("submit_planning_request", params)` is called
562	**Then** the correctly structured payload is sent to the Smartsheet API

564	**Given** the Smartsheet API returns a success response
565	**When** the tool call completes
566	**Then** the agent reports confirmation to the consultant in the chat panel (FR13)

568	**Given** the Smartsheet API is unavailable or returns an error
569	**When** `execute()` fails
570	**Then** `IntegrationError` is raised, caught at `app/api/`, and a specific plain-language message is returned — no partial execution of any dependent calendar action (FR16)

572	**Given** the tool call payload is logged
573	**When** the log entry is written
574	**Then** it contains `session_id`, `tool: "smartsheet"`, `latency_ms`, and `masked_input` — no identifiable consultant or client data (NFR7)

580	### Story 3.6: Google Calendar Integration
581	
582	As a **consultant**,
583	I want the agent to create Google Calendar invites around my existing engagements,

586	**Acceptance Criteria:**
587	
588	**Given** the consultant has confirmed a calendar action and the orchestration layer dispatches the registered Calendar tool
589	**When** `GoogleCalendarIntegration.execute("create_invite", params)` is called

594	**Then** the agent confirms the invite creation to the consultant in the chat panel

601	**When** the Smartsheet step succeeds but Calendar fails

603	
604	**Given** the tool call payload is logged
605	**When** the log entry is written
606	**Then** it contains `session_id`, `tool: "google_calendar"`, `latency_ms`, and `masked_input` — no identifiable consultant or client data (NFR7)

612	## Epic 4: Open Work Discovery & Acceptance _(POC Stretch Goal)_
613	
614	A consultant can browse open work opportunities (billable prioritised above internal), check their capacity against the commitment, accept or decline — with coordinator notification on acceptance and declined opportunities never resurfacing.

616	### Story 4.1: Open Work Board Ingestion & Display
617	
618	As a **consultant**,
619	I want to see open work opportunities from the org-wide board inside the extension panel, with billable work shown above internal projects,

622	**Acceptance Criteria:**
623	
624	**Given** an org-wide Google Doc URL is configured as the open work board
625	**When** the consultant opens the open work section of the panel

636	**Given** the open work board is ingested

640	**Dev notes:** FR7, FR8 — `GoogleDocsIntegration` called with org-wide board URL from workflow config; priority sort logic in agent layer, not UI

644	### Story 4.2: Capacity & Availability Check
645	
646	As a **consultant**,
647	I want the agent to tell me whether I can credibly commit to an open work opportunity before I decide,

650	**Acceptance Criteria:**
651

661	**When** the agent evaluates the opportunity
662	**Then** it flags the shortfall clearly — showing available days vs. required days including buffer — before asking if the consultant wants to proceed (FR9)

665	**When** the check runs

672	### Story 4.3: Accept / Decline Flow & Coordinator Notification
673	
674	As a **consultant**,

692	**Then** the previously declined opportunity is filtered out and never surfaced again (FR12)
693	
694	**Given** 80 consultants are accepting/declining concurrently
695	**When** `DeclinedOpportunity` records are written
696	**Then** async database writes complete without blocking the agent response (NFR11)
697	
698	**Given** the accept or decline action is logged
699	**When** the log entry is written
700	**Then** it contains `session_id`, `tool`, `latency_ms`, and `masked_input` — no consultant names or opportunity identifiers in plaintext (NFR7)
701	
702	**Dev notes:** FR10, FR11, FR12, ARC-11 — `DeclinedOpportunity` model + Alembic migration `0005_declined_opportunity.py` introduced here; coordinator notification tool registered in workflow config

# autom9 - Epic Breakdown

## Overview

This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for autom9, decomposing the requirements from the PRD and Architecture into implementable stories.

## Requirements Inventory

### Functional Requirements

FR1: Consultant can view their open days and scheduled engagements sourced from Snowflake via the Tableau data source within the extension panel
FR2: Consultant can view their task list ingested from their designated individual Google Doc
FR3: Consultant can interact with the AI agent via a chat interface embedded in the Tableau extension panel
FR4: Agent can ask clarifying questions about task timing, priority, and scheduling preferences before taking action
FR5: Agent retains context within a session to support multi-turn clarifying conversations
FR6: Consultant can review the agent's proposed actions before execution is confirmed
FR7: Agent surfaces open work opportunities from the org-wide Google Doc, distinguishing billable client work from internal projects
FR8: Agent prioritises billable opportunities above internal project opportunities
FR9: Agent calculates whether a consultant's available capacity meets the time commitment of an open work opportunity, including a 5% buffer
FR10: Consultant can accept or decline an open work opportunity from within the extension panel
FR11: Agent notifies the relevant coordinator when a consultant accepts an open work opportunity
FR12: Agent does not resurface a previously declined opportunity to the same consultant
FR13: Agent submits a Smartsheet planning request on behalf of the consultant
FR14: Agent creates Google Calendar invites for the consultant around existing engagements
FR15: Extension checks connectivity to all configured integrations on load and surfaces any unavailable services before interaction begins
FR16: Agent fails gracefully with a specific error message if an integration becomes unavailable during a workflow, without partially executing dependent actions
FR17: Agent masks identifiable data fields (names, client identifiers, engagement IDs) with opaque tokens before transmitting any context to the LLM provider
FR18: Agent rehydrates masked tokens with real values from the session token map before displaying output or executing tool actions
FR19: Integration credentials are never exposed in logs, the chat interface, or configuration files visible to consultants
FR20: Admin can install and register the extension in Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server
FR21: Admin can configure the BYOM LLM provider and API credentials at the org level via the extension configuration panel
FR22: Admin can load and update the JSON workflow configuration file defining agent capabilities, tool access, and workflow parameters
FR23: Admin can test integration connections from the configuration panel before activating the extension for consultants
FR24: Admin can access agent interaction logs with sufficient detail to diagnose failed tool calls, error patterns, and latency
FR25: Integration status check results are logged for admin review
FR26: New agent workflows can be added by updating the JSON workflow configuration file without modifying platform code
FR27: The JSON workflow configuration defines available tools, agent instructions, and workflow parameters in a versionable format
FR28: The extension supports OpenAI and Anthropic as BYOM LLM providers, switchable via configuration change
FR29: The extension is compatible with Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server

### NonFunctional Requirements

NFR1: Agent responses complete within 20 seconds (p95) under normal operating conditions during the POC phase (nice-to-have; no hard SLA in v1)
NFR2: The extension panel renders and integration status check completes within 5 seconds of Tableau dashboard load
NFR3: The chat interface displays a visible processing indicator within 1 second of the consultant submitting a message
NFR4: All data transmitted between the extension and external services is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+)
NFR5: API credentials and integration tokens are stored encrypted at rest and never surfaced in logs, UI elements, or configuration files accessible to consultants
NFR6: The token masking system transmits no real consultant names, client identifiers, or engagement IDs to any external LLM provider under any circumstances
NFR7: Agent interaction logs capture only masked data representations — no raw LLM payloads containing identifiable fields
NFR8: The extension identifies and reports unavailability of any configured integration within the 5-second load status check window
NFR9: A failure in one integration does not cascade to prevent other integrations from functioning
NFR10: The JSON workflow configuration system handles version mismatches gracefully — a config update does not break or corrupt an in-flight session
NFR11: The extension supports concurrent usage by all 80 POC consultants without degradation in agent response time
NFR12: The platform architecture imposes no design constraints that would prevent future multi-tenant isolation

### Additional Requirements

- **[ARC-1] Project Scaffolding (Day-Zero):** Backend scaffold: `uv init autom9-backend` with fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy[asyncio], asyncpg, alembic, pydantic-settings, python-jose, httpx, cryptography, python-json-logger. Frontend scaffold: `npm create vite@latest autom9-extension -- --template svelte-ts` with @tableau/extensions-api-types.
- **[ARC-2] .trex Manifest:** Create `autom9.trex` at extension project root with required fields: name, description, source-location (backend URL), min-version, permissions (read worksheets). Without this the extension cannot load for any testing.
- **[ARC-3] CORS Configuration:** Configure FastAPI `CORSMiddleware` in `main.py` with allowed Tableau origins (public.tableau.com and Tableau Server domain).
- **[ARC-4] JSON Workflow Config Schema:** Document schema in `app/config/workflow_schema.py` — minimum fields: version (semver), tools (array with name, description, parameters), agent_instructions (string), workflow_id (string).
- **[ARC-5] Tableau initializeAsync Gate:** `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` must complete before any store setup or backend calls in `App.svelte`.
- **[ARC-6] Alembic Fail-Fast:** Container must fail to start if migration fails. Enforced via Docker entrypoint exit code check.
- **[ARC-7] Async Test Setup:** `pytest.ini` must specify `asyncio_mode = auto`. Async SQLAlchemy fixtures must be function-scoped to prevent state leakage.
- **[ARC-8] Connection Pool Sizing:** `DATABASE_POOL_MIN` and `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` as environment variables (recommended: min=5, max=20) via pydantic-settings.
- **[ARC-9] masking.py Quality Gate:** `app/agent/masking.py` requires 100% branch coverage as a hard acceptance criterion for any story touching the agent pipeline.
- **[ARC-10] LLM Retry/Backoff Strategy:** `LLMProvider.complete()` must apply exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries max, then raise `ProviderError` on 429 or transient errors.
- **[ARC-11] Data Models:** Four core models required: `DeclinedOpportunity` (consultant_id, opportunity_id, declined_at), `InteractionLog` (session_id, masked_input, masked_output, tool_calls, latency_ms, timestamp), `CredentialStore` (org_id, provider, encrypted_key), `WorkflowConfig` (version, config_json, loaded_at), `Session` (session_id UUID PK, tableau_user_id, started_at).
- **[ARC-12] BYOM Provider Interface:** `LLMProvider` class with `complete()` and `stream()` — stream() raises `NotImplementedError` in v1.
- **[ARC-13] Integration Interface:** All integrations in `app/integrations/` implement `IntegrationBase` with `health_check()` and `execute()`. Failure raises `IntegrationError` caught at `app/api/` level.
- **[ARC-14] Session Registry:** `GET /api/admin/sessions/{session_id}` endpoint for admin triage. All `InteractionLog` entries reference session_id. PII stays out of logs.

### Story 3.6: Google Calendar Integration

As a **consultant**,
I want the agent to create Google Calendar invites around my existing engagements,
So that my calendar reflects my planned work without me manually scheduling each event.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the consultant has confirmed a calendar action and the orchestration layer dispatches the registered Calendar tool
**When** `GoogleCalendarIntegration.execute("create_invite", params)` is called
**Then** correctly structured event details (title, dates, times derived from engagement context) are sent to the Calendar API (FR14)

**Given** the Calendar API returns a success response
**When** the tool call completes
**Then** the agent confirms the invite creation to the consultant in the chat panel

**Given** the Calendar API is unavailable or the OAuth token has expired
**When** `execute()` fails
**Then** `IntegrationError` is raised with a specific error message identifying the Calendar integration — no partial execution of other pending actions (FR16)

**Given** a Calendar invite is created after a Smartsheet request in the same workflow
**When** the Smartsheet step succeeds but Calendar fails
**Then** the Smartsheet submission is not rolled back — each tool action is independent and the consultant is informed of the partial outcome with a specific message per integration (FR16)

**Given** the tool call payload is logged
**When** the log entry is written
**Then** it contains `session_id`, `tool: "google_calendar"`, `latency_ms`, and `masked_input` — no identifiable consultant or client data (NFR7)

**Dev notes:** FR14, FR16 — concrete `GoogleCalendarIntegration(IntegrationBase)` in `app/integrations/`; registered in the planning workflow JSON config by tool name

---

## Epic 4: Open Work Discovery & Acceptance _(POC Stretch Goal)_

A consultant can browse open work opportunities (billable prioritised above internal), check their capacity against the commitment, accept or decline — with coordinator notification on acceptance and declined opportunities never resurfacing.

### Story 4.1: Open Work Board Ingestion & Display

As a **consultant**,
I want to see open work opportunities from the org-wide board inside the extension panel, with billable work shown above internal projects,
So that I can quickly identify the highest-priority opportunities relevant to me.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an org-wide Google Doc URL is configured as the open work board
**When** the consultant opens the open work section of the panel
**Then** opportunities are ingested from the doc and displayed, each typed as `billable` or `internal` (FR7)

**Given** both billable and internal opportunities are present
**When** the list renders
**Then** all billable opportunities appear above all internal opportunities (FR8)

**Given** the org-wide Google Doc is unavailable
**When** ingestion fails
**Then** a specific plain-language error is shown — the rest of the extension panel remains functional (NFR9)

**Given** the open work board is ingested
**When** opportunities are displayed
**Then** the layout uses the same generic data rendering established in Story 3.1 — no new hardcoded UI structures for open work fields

**Dev notes:** FR7, FR8 — `GoogleDocsIntegration` called with org-wide board URL from workflow config; priority sort logic in agent layer, not UI

---

### Story 4.2: Capacity & Availability Check

As a **consultant**,
I want the agent to tell me whether I can credibly commit to an open work opportunity before I decide,
So that I don't accept work I don't have capacity for.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the consultant views an open work opportunity
**When** the agent evaluates it
**Then** it compares the consultant's available open days (from Tableau data) against the opportunity's time commitment plus a 5% buffer (FR9)

**Given** the consultant has sufficient capacity (open days ≥ time requested × 1.05)
**When** the agent surfaces the opportunity
**Then** it confirms the consultant can credibly commit and displays the capacity calculation

**Given** the consultant does not have sufficient capacity
**When** the agent evaluates the opportunity
**Then** it flags the shortfall clearly — showing available days vs. required days including buffer — before asking if the consultant wants to proceed (FR9)

**Given** the Tableau data source is unavailable when capacity is checked
**When** the check runs
**Then** `IntegrationError` is raised and the consultant is told capacity cannot be verified — the opportunity is not surfaced as committable (FR16)

**Dev notes:** FR9, FR16 — capacity calculation logic in `app/agent/`; uses open days already read via `tableau.ts` in Story 3.1

---

### Story 4.3: Accept / Decline Flow & Coordinator Notification

As a **consultant**,
I want to accept or decline an open work opportunity from the panel, with my decision logged and acted on immediately,
So that the coordinator is notified instantly on acceptance and I'm never shown an opportunity I've already declined.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an open work opportunity is displayed
**When** the consultant chooses to accept
**Then** the agent notifies the relevant coordinator (via the mechanism defined in the workflow config) (FR11)
**And** the acceptance is confirmed to the consultant in the chat panel

**Given** an open work opportunity is displayed
**When** the consultant declines
**Then** a `DeclinedOpportunity` record is persisted to the database (`consultant_id`, `opportunity_id`, `declined_at`) via Alembic migration introduced in this story (FR12, ARC-11)
**And** the agent acknowledges the decline without judgment and returns to idle

**Given** a `DeclinedOpportunity` record exists for a consultant+opportunity pair
**When** the open work board is next ingested for that consultant
**Then** the previously declined opportunity is filtered out and never surfaced again (FR12)

**Given** 80 consultants are accepting/declining concurrently
**When** `DeclinedOpportunity` records are written
**Then** async database writes complete without blocking the agent response (NFR11)

**Given** the accept or decline action is logged
**When** the log entry is written
**Then** it contains `session_id`, `tool`, `latency_ms`, and `masked_input` — no consultant names or opportunity identifiers in plaintext (NFR7)

**Dev notes:** FR10, FR11, FR12, ARC-11 — `DeclinedOpportunity` model + Alembic migration `0005_declined_opportunity.py` introduced here; coordinator notification tool registered in workflow config

40	**When** `health_check()` is called

44	**Given** credentials are configured but token refresh or the Docs API call fails

55	## ⚠️ CRITICAL PREREQUISITE — GoogleDocsIntegration Is a Stub

57	`app/integrations/google_docs.py` is **currently a stub** that always raises `IntegrationError`. Story 4.1 cannot be completed without implementing it. **Implementing the real `GoogleDocsIntegration` is the core deliverable of this story.** Everything else (config schema extension, endpoint, Svelte component, tests) builds on top of it.

59	The stub currently reads:

61	class GoogleDocsIntegration(IntegrationBase):
62	    async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus:
63	        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error="not configured")
64	
65	    async def execute(self, action: str, params: dict) -> dict:
66	        raise IntegrationError(self.name, "Google Docs not configured")

69	**Do NOT change the class interface (`IntegrationBase` contract, `name` property, `health_check`, `execute` signatures).** Only replace the stub bodies with real OAuth2 + Google Docs API calls.

73	## Tasks / Subtasks
74	
75	### [x] Task 1 — Add Google Docs OAuth credentials to `app/core/config.py`
76	
77	In `autom9-backend/app/core/config.py`, add four optional fields after `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID`:

81	GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET: str | None = None
82	GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN: str | None = None

90	
91	Replace the stub with a full implementation. **Mirror the `GoogleCalendarIntegration` pattern exactly** (`app/integrations/google_calendar.py`) — OAuth2 refresh token flow, double-checked locking, `asyncio.Lock` for token cache, `_credentials_present()`, `_missing_credential()`, `_get_access_token()` helpers.
92	
93	**OAuth endpoints:**
94	- Token refresh: `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` (same as Calendar)
95	- Docs API: `GET https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/{documentId}`
96	
97	**Document ID extraction:** Extract from URL with a helper:
98	```python
99	import re
100	_DOC_ID_RE = re.compile(r"/document/d/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)")
101	
102	def _extract_doc_id(url: str) -> str:
103	    m = _DOC_ID_RE.search(url)
104	    if not m:
105	        raise IntegrationError("google_docs", f"Cannot extract document ID from URL: {url}")
106	    return m.group(1)
107	```
108	
109	**`execute("fetch_tasks", {"url": "<google_docs_url>"})` contract:**
110	- Returns `{"tasks": [str, ...]}` — list of strings extracted from the document body
111	- Extract text from the Google Docs API response: iterate `document["body"]["content"]`, collect text from `paragraph.elements[].textRun.content` (skip non-textRun elements, strip whitespace, skip empty lines)
112	- Do NOT attempt to parse structure (billable vs internal) here — that belongs in `GET /api/data/open-work` (Task 3)
113	
114	**`execute("fetch_open_work", {"url": "<open_work_board_url>"})` contract:**
115	- Returns `{"opportunities": [{"title": str, "type": "billable"|"internal", ...remaining_fields}]}`
116	- Parse the document content to distinguish billable vs internal. Use a section-header detection heuristic: lines matching `^(Billable|Client Work)` (case-insensitive) open a billable section; lines matching `^(Internal|Internal Work)` open an internal section. All opportunity lines within a section inherit that type.
117	- Each opportunity: `{"title": str, "type": "billable"|"internal", "details": str}` — `details` is the raw line text
118	- Lines that don't match any section header and aren't blank are treated as opportunities under the current section (default: `"internal"` if no section header seen yet)
119	
120	**`health_check()` implementation:**
121	1. Check `_credentials_present()` → return `unavailable` with specific missing credential name
122	2. Attempt `_get_access_token()` in a try/except
123	3. If token acquired, make a minimal Docs API probe call (use a well-known test doc ID or the token introspection endpoint) — OR simply validate the token was returned without an API call to minimize blast radius during health check
124	4. Wrap entire method in try/except; return `unavailable` with error message — NEVER raise (same contract as every other `health_check`)

229	- `test_fetch_open_work_all_internal` — all items typed internal

266	```
267	
268	---
269	
270	## Architecture Compliance
271	
272	### Must Follow — No Exceptions
273	
274	- **IntegrationBase contract:** `health_check()` NEVER raises; `execute()` raises `IntegrationError` on failure — never bare `Exception`
275	- **IntegrationError signature:** `IntegrationError(self.name, "<message>")` — matches `app/core/exceptions.py` constructor
276	- **Registry-driven health check:** `GoogleDocsIntegration` is already in `ALL_INTEGRATIONS` via `app/integrations/__init__.py` — the existing health check endpoint will automatically pick up the real implementation. Verify it is registered there; if not, add it.
277	- **NFR9 — independent failure isolation:** `OpenWorkPanel` failure must not cascade. `Promise.allSettled` pattern if fetching alongside other panels concurrently.
278	- **No hardcoded field names in UI:** `OpenWorkPanel` renders from data keys, not planning-specific labels
279	- **`{data: ..., meta: {request_id}}` response envelope:** `OpenWorkResponse` must use the existing `Meta` schema from `app/schemas/status.py`
280	- **snake_case everywhere:** API response keys, DB column names, Python identifiers
281	- **ARC-9 gate:** `app/agent/masking.py` is NOT touched in this story. If any change to the masking pipeline is needed, check with the SM first. ARC-9 100% branch coverage must not regress.
282	
283	### File Locations — Do Not Deviate
284	
285	| What | Where |
286	|------|-------|
287	| Google Docs credentials | `app/core/config.py` — after `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID` |
288	| GoogleDocsIntegration | `app/integrations/google_docs.py` — replace stub bodies |
289	| WorkflowConfigSchema change | `app/config/workflow_schema.py` |
290	| New endpoint | `app/api/data.py` — add to existing router |
291	| New schemas | `app/schemas/data.py` — add to existing file |
292	| OpenWorkPanel | `autom9-extension/src/components/OpenWorkPanel.svelte` |
293	| Integration tests | `autom9-backend/tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py` |
294	| API tests | `autom9-backend/tests/api/test_open_work.py` |
295	
296	---
297	
298	## Previous Story Intelligence (from Story 3.6 — GoogleCalendarIntegration)
299	
300	The `GoogleCalendarIntegration` implementation is the canonical reference for this story. Key patterns to carry forward verbatim:
301	
302	**Double-checked locking for token cache:**
303	```python
304	async def _get_access_token(self) -> str:
305	    if self._access_token and time.monotonic() < self._token_expiry:
306	        return self._access_token
307	    async with self._token_lock:
308	        if self._access_token and time.monotonic() < self._token_expiry:
309	            return self._access_token
310	        # ... refresh ...
311	```
312	
313	**Token expiry with buffer:**
314	```python
315	self._token_expiry = time.monotonic() + data["expires_in"] - _TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_SECS
316	```
317	
318	**`health_check()` wraps everything in try/except:**
319	```python
320	async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus:
321	    if not self._credentials_present():
322	        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error=f"{self._missing_credential()} not set")
323	    try:
324	        start = time.monotonic()
325	        await self._get_access_token()
326	        # optional probe call
327	        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
328	        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="healthy", latency_ms=latency_ms)
329	    except Exception as exc:
330	        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error=str(exc))
331	```
332	
333	**Review findings from 3.6 to avoid in this story:**
334	- AC5 log compliance: include `session_id` and `latency_ms` in endpoint-level logs (the integration-level log from `_handle_confirm` handles `masked_input` — the data endpoint logs `session_id` and `integration` name only, which is the established pattern from `GET /api/data/tasks`)
335	- No action registry/enum: story 4.1 only uses `fetch_open_work` action — dispatch table deferral from 3.6 deferred-work applies here too
336	
337	---
338	
339	## Key Decisions & Constraints
340	
341	**Why `fetch_open_work` as a separate action from `fetch_tasks`:**
342	The existing `fetch_tasks` action (used by `GET /api/data/tasks`) returns `{"tasks": [str]}` — a flat list. Open work opportunities have structure (`title`, `type`, `details`). Reusing the same action would require breaking the existing schema. The integration supports both actions; `fetch_tasks` continues to serve `GET /api/data/tasks`, `fetch_open_work` serves `GET /api/data/open-work`.
343	
344	**Why sort server-side (Task 3, not frontend):**
345	The epic spec dev notes explicitly state: "priority sort logic in agent layer, not UI." The endpoint sorts before returning. The frontend renders in order received.

# Story 4.1: Open Work Board Ingestion & Display

Status: done

## Story

As a **consultant**,
I want to see open work opportunities from the org-wide board inside the extension panel, with billable work shown above internal projects,
So that I can quickly identify the highest-priority opportunities relevant to me.

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1 — Happy path: opportunities displayed**
**Given** an org-wide Google Doc URL is configured as the open work board (`workflow_config.open_work_board.google_docs_url`)
**When** the consultant opens the open work section of the panel
**Then** opportunities are ingested from the doc and displayed, each typed as `billable` or `internal` (FR7)

**AC2 — Billable above internal**
**Given** both billable and internal opportunities are present
**When** the list renders
**Then** all billable opportunities appear above all internal opportunities — sort is applied server-side in `GET /api/data/open-work`, not in the UI (FR8)

**AC3 — Integration failure isolation**
**Given** the org-wide Google Doc is unavailable or the URL is not configured
**When** ingestion fails
**Then** a specific plain-language error is shown in the open work section — the rest of the extension panel (StatusBar, DataPanel, ChatPanel) remains fully functional (NFR9)

**AC4 — Generic rendering**
**Given** the open work board is ingested
**When** opportunities are displayed
**Then** the layout uses the same generic list rendering established in Story 3.1 (`DataPanel.svelte` pattern) — no new hardcoded UI structures for open work fields; field names are driven by data keys

**AC5 — Health check: not configured**
**Given** `GoogleDocsIntegration.health_check()` is called
**When** `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET`, or `GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN` is not set
**Then** `IntegrationStatus(name="google_docs", status="unavailable", error="<specific credential name> not set")` is returned without making any HTTP call

**AC6 — Health check: configured and reachable**
**Given** all credentials are set and the Docs API is reachable
**When** `health_check()` is called
**Then** `IntegrationStatus(name="google_docs", status="healthy", latency_ms=<N>)` is returned

**AC7 — Health check: credentials present but API unreachable**
**Given** credentials are configured but token refresh or the Docs API call fails
**When** `health_check()` runs
**Then** `IntegrationStatus(name="google_docs", status="unavailable", error="<specific message>")` is returned — `health_check()` NEVER raises

**AC8 — Log masking**
**Given** the open work fetch is logged
**When** the log entry is written
**Then** it contains `session_id`, `integration: "google_docs"`, and no identifiable opportunity, client, or consultant data — consistent with existing `GET /api/data/tasks` log pattern (NFR7)

---

## ⚠️ CRITICAL PREREQUISITE — GoogleDocsIntegration Is a Stub

`app/integrations/google_docs.py` is **currently a stub** that always raises `IntegrationError`. Story 4.1 cannot be completed without implementing it. **Implementing the real `GoogleDocsIntegration` is the core deliverable of this story.** Everything else (config schema extension, endpoint, Svelte component, tests) builds on top of it.

The stub currently reads:
```python
class GoogleDocsIntegration(IntegrationBase):
    async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus:
        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error="not configured")

    async def execute(self, action: str, params: dict) -> dict:
        raise IntegrationError(self.name, "Google Docs not configured")
```

**Do NOT change the class interface (`IntegrationBase` contract, `name` property, `health_check`, `execute` signatures).** Only replace the stub bodies with real OAuth2 + Google Docs API calls.

---

## Tasks / Subtasks

### [x] Task 1 — Add Google Docs OAuth credentials to `app/core/config.py`

In `autom9-backend/app/core/config.py`, add four optional fields after `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID`:

```python
GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID: str | None = None
GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET: str | None = None
GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN: str | None = None
```

No validator needed — `None` is the valid "not configured" state. The integration checks for `None` itself (same pattern as `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID`).

---

### [x] Task 2 — Implement real `GoogleDocsIntegration` in `app/integrations/google_docs.py`

Replace the stub with a full implementation. **Mirror the `GoogleCalendarIntegration` pattern exactly** (`app/integrations/google_calendar.py`) — OAuth2 refresh token flow, double-checked locking, `asyncio.Lock` for token cache, `_credentials_present()`, `_missing_credential()`, `_get_access_token()` helpers.

**OAuth endpoints:**
- Token refresh: `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` (same as Calendar)
- Docs API: `GET https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/{documentId}`

**Document ID extraction:** Extract from URL with a helper:
```python
import re
_DOC_ID_RE = re.compile(r"/document/d/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)")

def _extract_doc_id(url: str) -> str:
    m = _DOC_ID_RE.search(url)
    if not m:
        raise IntegrationError("google_docs", f"Cannot extract document ID from URL: {url}")
    return m.group(1)
```

**`execute("fetch_tasks", {"url": "<google_docs_url>"})` contract:**
- Returns `{"tasks": [str, ...]}` — list of strings extracted from the document body
- Extract text from the Google Docs API response: iterate `document["body"]["content"]`, collect text from `paragraph.elements[].textRun.content` (skip non-textRun elements, strip whitespace, skip empty lines)
- Do NOT attempt to parse structure (billable vs internal) here — that belongs in `GET /api/data/open-work` (Task 3)

**`execute("fetch_open_work", {"url": "<open_work_board_url>"})` contract:**
- Returns `{"opportunities": [{"title": str, "type": "billable"|"internal", ...remaining_fields}]}`
- Parse the document content to distinguish billable vs internal. Use a section-header detection heuristic: lines matching `^(Billable|Client Work)` (case-insensitive) open a billable section; lines matching `^(Internal|Internal Work)` open an internal section. All opportunity lines within a section inherit that type.
- Each opportunity: `{"title": str, "type": "billable"|"internal", "details": str}` — `details` is the raw line text
- Lines that don't match any section header and aren't blank are treated as opportunities under the current section (default: `"internal"` if no section header seen yet)

**`health_check()` implementation:**
1. Check `_credentials_present()` → return `unavailable` with specific missing credential name
2. Attempt `_get_access_token()` in a try/except
3. If token acquired, make a minimal Docs API probe call (use a well-known test doc ID or the token introspection endpoint) — OR simply validate the token was returned without an API call to minimize blast radius during health check
4. Wrap entire method in try/except; return `unavailable` with error message — NEVER raise (same contract as every other `health_check`)

**Module constants (match Calendar pattern):**
```python
_TOKEN_ENDPOINT = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
_DOCS_API_BASE = "https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents"
_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_SECS = 60
```

**httpx usage:** Always use `async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:` — no global client instance (same as Calendar).

---

### [x] Task 3 — Extend `WorkflowConfigSchema` with `open_work_board` section

In `autom9-backend/app/config/workflow_schema.py`, add an `OpenWorkBoardConfig` model and optional field on `WorkflowConfigSchema`. Mirror the existing `DataPanelConfig` pattern exactly:

```python
class OpenWorkBoardConfig(BaseModel):
    google_docs_url: str  # required — no org-wide URL = no open work board


class WorkflowConfigSchema(BaseModel):
    # ... existing fields ...
    data_panel: DataPanelConfig | None = None
    open_work_board: OpenWorkBoardConfig | None = None  # ADD THIS
```

`open_work_board` is optional at the schema level so that existing workflow configs without it remain valid (NFR10 — no config update breaks in-flight sessions). The endpoint handles the `None` case with a 404.

---

### [x] Task 4 — Add `GET /api/data/open-work` endpoint to `app/api/data.py`

Add a new route to the **existing** `autom9-backend/app/api/data.py` module. Do NOT create a new file.

**Request:** `GET /api/data/open-work` with optional `X-Autom9-Session` header (same pattern as `GET /api/data/tasks`)

**Response schema** — add to `autom9-backend/app/schemas/data.py`:

```python
class OpportunityItem(BaseModel):
    title: str
    type: Literal["billable", "internal"]
    details: str

class OpenWorkResponse(BaseModel):
    data: list[OpportunityItem]
    meta: Meta
```

**Endpoint logic:**
1. Read `workflow_registry.active_config` → 404 if None
2. Read `active_config.get("open_work_board")` → 404 if None or no `google_docs_url`
3. Log fetch attempt: `{"session_id": ..., "integration": "google_docs"}`
4. Call `_google_docs.execute("fetch_open_work", {"url": google_docs_url})`
5. On `IntegrationError` → log warning → raise `HTTPException(status_code=503)`
6. Sort result: `billable` items first, `internal` items second (stable sort preserving order within each group)
7. Return `OpenWorkResponse(data=[...], meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid4())))`

**Module-level singleton:** reuse the existing `_google_docs = GoogleDocsIntegration()` already present at module level — do NOT add a second singleton.

**Import additions needed:** `Literal` from typing, `OpportunityItem`, `OpenWorkResponse` from `app.schemas.data`.

---

### [x] Task 5 — Add `OpenWorkPanel.svelte` frontend component

Create `autom9-extension/src/components/OpenWorkPanel.svelte`.

**Pattern to follow:** `DataPanel.svelte` (Story 3.1) — same `apiFetch` call, same error handling, same generic list rendering. Do NOT hardcode field names.

**Key differences from DataPanel:**
- Endpoint: `GET /api/data/open-work`
- Type badge: each item has a `type` field (`"billable"` or `"internal"`) — render a small badge/label next to the title (e.g. `[Billable]` or `[Internal]`)
- Sort is already applied server-side — render items in the order returned
- Section is independent of `DataPanel` — failure in `OpenWorkPanel` does not affect `DataPanel` rendering

**Svelte 5 syntax:** use `$state`, `$derived`, runes pattern (same as existing components). No Svelte 4 `let:` or reactive `$:` syntax.

**Data fetch:** call on component mount (`$effect`). Set loading/error/data states. No abort controller required for v1 (same deferral as DataPanel — see deferred-work.md for prior precedent).

**Integration into `App.svelte`:** Add `<OpenWorkPanel />` import and render it below `<DataPanel />` in the extension layout. Do not restructure existing layout logic.

---

### [x] Task 6 — Tests

#### `tests/integrations/test_google_docs.py` (new file)

Structure mirrors `tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py` exactly (use it as the reference). Required coverage:

**health_check — not configured (per credential):**
- `test_health_check_no_client_id` — missing `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID`
- `test_health_check_no_client_secret` — missing `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `test_health_check_no_refresh_token` — missing `GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN`

**health_check — configured:**
- `test_health_check_ok` — successful token refresh + healthy result
- `test_health_check_token_refresh_fails` — non-200 from token endpoint → `unavailable`
- `test_health_check_docs_api_unreachable` (if health_check makes a probe call) — `httpx.RequestError` → `unavailable`

**execute fetch_open_work — happy paths:**
- `test_fetch_open_work_billable_above_internal` — mixed doc content returns billable before internal
- `test_fetch_open_work_all_billable` — all items typed billable
- `test_fetch_open_work_all_internal` — all items typed internal
- `test_fetch_open_work_empty_doc` — empty doc body → `{"opportunities": []}`

**execute fetch_open_work — failure paths:**
- `test_fetch_open_work_bad_url` — URL with no doc ID → `IntegrationError`
- `test_fetch_open_work_docs_api_error` — non-200 response → `IntegrationError`
- `test_fetch_open_work_token_refresh_fails` — token refresh fails → `IntegrationError`
- `test_fetch_open_work_invalid_json` — malformed API response → `IntegrationError`

**execute fetch_tasks (existing action, now real):**
- `test_fetch_tasks_returns_text_list` — confirms `{"tasks": [...]}` format still works

**Monkeypatch pattern** (mirror Calendar test exactly):
```python
def _configured(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr("app.integrations.google_docs.settings.GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID", "cid")
    monkeypatch.setattr("app.integrations.google_docs.settings.GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET", "cs")
    monkeypatch.setattr("app.integrations.google_docs.settings.GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN", "rt")
```

#### `tests/api/test_open_work.py` (new file)

Mirror `tests/api/test_data.py` pattern. Required cases:

- `test_get_open_work_no_config_returns_404`
- `test_get_open_work_no_open_work_board_returns_404`
- `test_get_open_work_no_google_docs_url_returns_404`
- `test_get_open_work_integration_unavailable_returns_503`
- `test_get_open_work_returns_opportunities_sorted_billable_first`
- `test_get_open_work_session_header_forwarded`

**Mock pattern for integration:** use `monkeypatch.setattr(data_module, "_google_docs", mock_integration)` where `mock_integration.execute = AsyncMock(return_value={"opportunities": [...]})` — same approach as existing data tests.

#### File headers (required in all new test files):
```python
import pytest
pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="session")
```

---

## Architecture Compliance

### Must Follow — No Exceptions

- **IntegrationBase contract:** `health_check()` NEVER raises; `execute()` raises `IntegrationError` on failure — never bare `Exception`
- **IntegrationError signature:** `IntegrationError(self.name, "<message>")` — matches `app/core/exceptions.py` constructor
- **Registry-driven health check:** `GoogleDocsIntegration` is already in `ALL_INTEGRATIONS` via `app/integrations/__init__.py` — the existing health check endpoint will automatically pick up the real implementation. Verify it is registered there; if not, add it.
- **NFR9 — independent failure isolation:** `OpenWorkPanel` failure must not cascade. `Promise.allSettled` pattern if fetching alongside other panels concurrently.
- **No hardcoded field names in UI:** `OpenWorkPanel` renders from data keys, not planning-specific labels
- **`{data: ..., meta: {request_id}}` response envelope:** `OpenWorkResponse` must use the existing `Meta` schema from `app/schemas/status.py`
- **snake_case everywhere:** API response keys, DB column names, Python identifiers
- **ARC-9 gate:** `app/agent/masking.py` is NOT touched in this story. If any change to the masking pipeline is needed, check with the SM first. ARC-9 100% branch coverage must not regress.

## Previous Story Intelligence (from Story 3.6 — GoogleCalendarIntegration)

The `GoogleCalendarIntegration` implementation is the canonical reference for this story. Key patterns to carry forward verbatim:

**Double-checked locking for token cache:**
```python
async def _get_access_token(self) -> str:
    if self._access_token and time.monotonic() < self._token_expiry:
        return self._access_token
    async with self._token_lock:
        if self._access_token and time.monotonic() < self._token_expiry:
            return self._access_token
        # ... refresh ...
```

**Token expiry with buffer:**
```python
self._token_expiry = time.monotonic() + data["expires_in"] - _TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_SECS
```

**`health_check()` wraps everything in try/except:**
```python
async def health_check(self) -> IntegrationStatus:
    if not self._credentials_present():
        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error=f"{self._missing_credential()} not set")
    try:
        start = time.monotonic()
        await self._get_access_token()
        # optional probe call
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="healthy", latency_ms=latency_ms)
    except Exception as exc:
        return IntegrationStatus(name=self.name, status="unavailable", error=str(exc))
```

**Review findings from 3.6 to avoid in this story:**
- AC5 log compliance: include `session_id` and `latency_ms` in endpoint-level logs (the integration-level log from `_handle_confirm` handles `masked_input` — the data endpoint logs `session_id` and `integration` name only, which is the established pattern from `GET /api/data/tasks`)
- No action registry/enum: story 4.1 only uses `fetch_open_work` action — dispatch table deferral from 3.6 deferred-work applies here too

## Key Decisions & Constraints

**Why `fetch_open_work` as a separate action from `fetch_tasks`:**
The existing `fetch_tasks` action (used by `GET /api/data/tasks`) returns `{"tasks": [str]}` — a flat list. Open work opportunities have structure (`title`, `type`, `details`). Reusing the same action would require breaking the existing schema. The integration supports both actions; `fetch_tasks` continues to serve `GET /api/data/tasks`, `fetch_open_work` serves `GET /api/data/open-work`.

**Why sort server-side (Task 3, not frontend):**
The epic spec dev notes explicitly state: "priority sort logic in agent layer, not UI." The endpoint sorts before returning. The frontend renders in order received.

**Google Docs API — document structure note:**
The Google Docs REST API (`GET https://docs.googleapis.com/v1/documents/{documentId}`) returns a deeply nested JSON structure. The relevant path for text is:
```
document.body.content[] → paragraph.elements[] → textRun.content (str)
```
Non-textRun elements (e.g. `inlineObjectElement`) must be skipped. Empty or whitespace-only strings must be filtered.

**Billable vs internal parsing heuristic:**
This is a POC. The heuristic (section headers) is good enough for v1. If the org-wide Google Doc uses a different structure, the admin can update the doc format to match — this is not a platform constraint. Document the heuristic assumption in a comment in the implementation.

**`OpenWorkPanel` is not wired into the agent chat (Story 4.1 scope):**
Story 4.1 delivers display only. Agent interaction with open work opportunities (capacity check, accept/decline) is Stories 4.2 and 4.3. `OpenWorkPanel` must render data but does not need to send messages to `chatStore`.
